title.zh: 卷一百六十五 列傳第五十二: 張禧 賈文備 解誠 管如德 趙匣剌 周全 孔元 朱國寶 張立 齊秉節 張萬家奴 郭昂 綦公直 楊賽因不花 鮮卑仲吉 完顏石柱
title.en: Volume 165 Biographies 52: Zhang Xi, Jia Wenbei, Jie Cheng, Guan Rude, Zhao Xiala, Zhou Quan, Kong Yuan, Zhu Guobao, Zhang Li, Qi Bingjie, Zhangwan Jianu, Guo Ang, Qi Gongzhi, Yangsaiyinbuhua, Xianbei Zhongji, Wanyan Shizhu

sentences.zh: 張禧，東安州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Xi was a native of Dong'an prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xi came from Dong'an prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父仁義，金末徙家益都。

translations.literal: His father Renyi moved the family to Yidu at the end of the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Renyi had relocated the household to Yidu in the Jin dynasty's final years.

sentences.zh: 及太宗下山東，仁義乃走信安。

translations.literal: When Taizong descended upon Shandong, Renyi then fled to Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong's armies overran Shandong, Renyi fled to Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 時燕薊已下，獨信安猶為金守，其主將知仁義勇而有謀，用之左右。

translations.literal: At that time Yan and Ji had already fallen; only Xin'an was still held for Jin. Its commanding general knew Renyi was brave and resourceful, and employed him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yan and the Ji region had already submitted, and Xin'an alone remained in Jin hands. The city commandant, recognizing Renyi's courage and cunning, kept him close as an adviser.

sentences.zh: 國兵圍信安，仁義率敢死士三百，開門出戰，圍解，以功署軍馬總管。

translations.literal: The imperial army besieged Xin'an. Renyi led three hundred dare-to-die troops, opened the gates and fought out; the siege was lifted, and for this merit he was appointed commander of army mounts.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial forces besieged Xin'an, Renyi led three hundred volunteers in a sortie through the gates and broke the encirclement. For this exploit he was made commander of army mounts.

sentences.zh: 守信安逾十年，度不能支，乃與主將舉城內附。

translations.literal: He held Xin'an for more than ten years; estimating that he could not sustain it, he then together with the commanding general brought the whole city to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He held Xin'an for more than a decade, but seeing that resistance could not last, he and the commandant submitted the city to the new dynasty.

sentences.zh: 率其部曲從宗王合醜平定河南，授管軍元帥。

translations.literal: Leading his household troops he followed Prince Hechou in pacifying Henan, and was appointed commander-in-chief of governing troops.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince Hechou with his personal following to pacify Henan and was appointed an army commander.

sentences.zh: 後攻歸德，飛矢入口，折其二齒，鏃出項後，卒，賜爵縣侯。

translations.literal: Later when attacking Guide, a stray arrow entered his mouth, broke two of his teeth, and the arrowhead emerged from the back of his neck. He died, and was granted the rank of marquis of a county.
translations.idiomatic: Later, during the assault on Guide, an arrow struck him in the mouth, snapping two teeth before its head exited the back of his neck. He died and was posthumously ennobled as a county marquis.

sentences.zh: 禧年十六，從大將軍阿術魯南攻徐州、歸德，復從元帥察罕攻壽春、安豐、廬、滁、黃、泗諸州，皆有功。

translations.literal: When Xi was sixteen, he followed the great general Artsur south to attack Xuzhou and Guide; he again followed Marshal Chaghan to attack Shouchun, Anfeng, Lu, Chu, Huang, and Si prefectures, and in all had merit.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen, Xi campaigned south under the great general Artsur at Xuzhou and Guide, then served under Marshal Chaghan at Shouchun, Anfeng, Lu, Chu, Huang, and Si, distinguishing himself in each engagement.

sentences.zh: 禧素峭直，為主將所忌，誣以他罪，欲置之法。

translations.literal: Xi had always been stern and upright; the commanding general resented him, falsely accused him of other crimes, and wished to execute him by law.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was by nature blunt and upright; his commander took offense, trumped up charges, and sought his execution.

sentences.zh: 時王鶚侍世祖於潛邸，禧密往依之，鶚請左丞闊闊薦禧與其子弘綱俱入見。

translations.literal: At that time Wang He attended the future Emperor Shizu at the Hidden Residence. Xi secretly went to rely on him; Wang He asked the left vice premier Kuoku to recommend Xi and his son Honggang to enter together for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Wang He was then attending the future Kublai Khan at his princely residence; Xi fled to him in secret, and Wang He had the left vice premier Kuoku present Xi and his son Honggang at court.

sentences.zh: 歲己未，從世祖南伐，濟江，與宋兵始接戰，即擒其一將。

translations.literal: In the year jiwei, he followed Emperor Shizu on the southern campaign, crossed the river, and at the first engagement with Song troops immediately captured one of their generals.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiwei year (1259) he accompanied Kublai Khan's southern expedition. After crossing the Yangzi he met Song forces in their first clash and captured a general at once.

sentences.zh: 進攻鄂州，諸軍穴城以入，宋樹柵為夾城於內，入戰者輒不利，乃命以厚賞募敢死士。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Ezhou, the armies tunneled into the city walls; the Song planted palisades as an inner double wall. Those who entered to fight invariably fared badly, so an order was given to recruit dare-to-die troops with rich rewards.
translations.idiomatic: At the assault on Ezhou the besiegers mined the walls, but the Song built an inner palisade line. Assault troops met repeated reverses, and commanders offered heavy bounties for volunteers.

sentences.zh: 禧與子弘綱俱應募，由城東南入戰，將至城下，帝憫其父子俱入險地，遣阿里海牙諭禧父子，止一人進戰。

translations.literal: Xi and his son Honggang both volunteered; they entered battle from the southeast of the city. As they were about to reach the wall, the Emperor pitied father and son both entering peril, and sent Alai Haiya to instruct the Xi father and son that only one should advance to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and Honggang both volunteered and attacked from the southeast. Seeing father and son both in the thick of danger, the Khan sent Alai Haiya to tell them only one should press the assault.

sentences.zh: 禧所執槍中弩矢而折，取弘綱槍以入，破城東南角。

translations.literal: The spear Xi wielded was struck by a crossbow bolt and broke; he took Honggang's spear and entered, breaching the southeast corner of the wall.
translations.idiomatic: A crossbow bolt shattered his spear; he seized Honggang's and broke through the southeast corner of the defenses.

sentences.zh: 有逗留不進者十餘人，立城下，弘綱复奪其槍入。

translations.literal: More than ten men who lingered and would not advance stood below the wall; Honggang again seized their spears and entered.
translations.idiomatic: A dozen hesitant men hung back at the foot of the wall; Honggang seized their spears from them and charged in again.

sentences.zh: 轉戰良久，禧身中十八矢，一矢鏃貫腹，悶絕復甦，曰：「得血竭飲之，血出可生。」

translations.literal: After fighting for a long time, Xi was struck by eighteen arrows; one arrowhead pierced through his belly. He fainted and revived, saying: "If dragon's-blood resin is obtained to drink, when the blood flows out I can live."
translations.idiomatic: After prolonged fighting Xi had taken eighteen wounds; one shaft transfixed his abdomen. He lost consciousness, then revived and said, "Fetch dragon's-blood resin to drink—once the blood drains I can survive."

sentences.zh: 世祖亟命取血竭，遣人往療之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu urgently ordered dragon's-blood resin to be fetched and sent someone to treat him.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai Khan immediately ordered the resin brought and sent physicians to treat him.

sentences.zh: 瘡既愈，復從大將納剌忽與宋兵戰於金口、李家洲，皆捷。

translations.literal: When his wounds had healed, he again followed the great general Nalahu to fight Song troops at Jinkou and Lijia Isle, and in both was victorious.
translations.idiomatic: Once healed he rejoined the general Nalahu and won victories over Song forces at Jinkou and Lijia Isle.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，賜金符，授新軍千戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu took the throne, he was granted a gold tally and appointed chiliarch of the New Army.
translations.idiomatic: At Kublai's accession he received a gold tally and was made chiliarch of a new army unit.

sentences.zh: 三年，從征李璮。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed the campaign against Li Tan.
translations.idiomatic: In year three of the reign he marched against Li Tan's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 時宋乘璮叛，遣夏貴襲取蘄縣、宿州等城，禧移兵攻之，貴走，盡复諸城。

translations.literal: At that time Song, taking advantage of Li Tan's rebellion, sent Xia Gui to raid and seize Qixian, Suzhou, and other cities. Xi moved troops to attack them; Gui fled and all the cities were fully recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The Song seized the moment of Li Tan's revolt to send Xia Gui against Qixian, Suzhou, and neighboring towns. Xi counterattacked, drove Gui off, and recovered every city.

sentences.zh: 至元元年，升唐鄧等州盧氏保甲丁壯軍總管。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiyuan he was promoted to commander of the militia and able-bodied troops of Lushi in Tang, Deng, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 1 (1264) he was promoted to commander of the Lushi militia levy in Tang, Deng, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 宋侵均州，總管李玉山敗走，帝命禧代之。

translations.literal: Song invaded Jun prefecture; Commander Li Yushan was defeated and fled. The Emperor ordered Xi to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Song forces invaded Junzhou, Commander Li Yushan was routed, and the Emperor sent Xi to take his place.

sentences.zh: 三年，與宋將呂文煥戰於高頭赤山，乘勝复均州。

translations.literal: In the third year he fought with the Song general Lü Wenhuan at Gaotouchi Mountain, and following up his victory recovered Jun prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he defeated the Song general Lü Wenhuan at Gaotouchi Mountain and, pressing the advantage, retook Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，改水軍總管，益其軍二千五百，令習水戰。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was changed to commander of the naval forces, his army was increased by two thousand five hundred, and he was ordered to practice naval warfare.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he was made naval commander, given another twenty-five hundred troops, and ordered to train them for river combat.

sentences.zh: 五年，從攻襄樊。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed the attack on Xiangyang and Fancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he joined the siege of Xiangyang and Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 六年七月，夏貴率兵援襄陽，禧從元帥阿術戰，卻之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year Xia Gui led troops to relieve Xiangyang; Xi followed Marshal Aju into battle and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year six Xia Gui marched to relieve Xiangyang; Xi fought under Marshal Aju and drove him back.

sentences.zh: 八年，江水暴溢，宋遣範文虎以戰艦千餘艘來援。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the river waters suddenly overflowed; Song sent Fan Wenhuge with more than a thousand warships to relieve the city.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight a flood swelled the Han River, and the Song sent Fan Wenhuge with over a thousand warships to break the siege.

sentences.zh: 元帥阿術命禧率輕舟，夜銜枚入其陣中，插葦以識水之深淺。

translations.literal: Marshal Aju ordered Xi to lead light boats; at night with gag-sticks in their mouths they entered the enemy formation and planted reeds to mark the depth of the water.
translations.idiomatic: Marshal Aju sent Xi with light craft to probe the enemy line by night, gag-sticks silencing the crews as they planted reeds to mark the channel depths.

sentences.zh: 及還，阿術即命禧率四翼水軍進戰，宋兵潰，追至淺水，奪戰艦七十餘艘。

translations.literal: When they returned, Aju at once ordered Xi to lead the four-wing naval force into battle; Song troops were routed, pursued to shallow water, and more than seventy warships were captured.
translations.idiomatic: On their return Aju sent Xi with the four naval wings into action. The Song fleet broke; pursued into the shallows, they lost more than seventy warships.

sentences.zh: 九年，攻樊城，焚其串樓，敗宋將張貴於鹿門山。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he attacked Fancheng, burned its chained towers, and defeated the Song general Zhang Gui at Lumen Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine he assaulted Fancheng, burned its siege towers, and routed the Song general Zhang Gui at Lumen Mountain.

sentences.zh: 十年，行省集諸將問破襄陽之策，禧言：「襄、樊夾漢江而城，敵人橫鐵鎖、置木橛於水中，今斷鎖毀橛，以絕其援，則樊城必下。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the regional secretariat assembled the generals to ask plans for taking Xiangyang. Xi said: "Xiang and Fan are walled on either side of the Han River. The enemy has stretched iron chains and set wooden stakes in the water. If we now sever the chains and destroy the stakes to cut off their relief, Fancheng will certainly fall.
translations.idiomatic: In year ten the regional command gathered its generals for a plan to crack Xiangyang. Xi argued: "Xiangyang and Fancheng face each other across the Han, with iron chains and stakes blocking the river. Cut the chains, smash the stakes, and relief cannot reach them—Fancheng will fall.

sentences.zh: 樊城下，則襄陽可圖矣。」

translations.literal: When Fancheng falls, then Xiangyang can be taken in view."
translations.idiomatic: Once Fancheng is taken, Xiangyang will follow."

sentences.zh: 行省用其計，乃破樊城，而襄陽繼降。

translations.literal: The regional secretariat adopted his plan, and thus broke Fancheng, while Xiangyang then surrendered in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The command adopted his plan, took Fancheng, and Xiangyang surrendered soon after.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使錄諸將功，授宣武將軍、水軍萬戶，佩金虎符，丞相伯顏因命禧為水軍先鋒。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent envoys to record the generals' merits; Xi was appointed General of Manifest Martiality and naval forces ten-thousand-household, wearing a gold tiger tally; Chancellor Bayan therefore ordered Xi to be vanguard of the naval forces.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor dispatched clerks to record each general's merit. Xi was made General of Manifest Martiality and naval ten-thousand-household, with a gold tiger tally, and Chancellor Bayan named him vanguard of the fleet.

sentences.zh: 十二年，敗宋將孫虎臣於丁家洲，尋移屯黃池，以斷宋救兵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he defeated the Song general Sun Huchen at Dingjia Isle, then moved camp to Huangchi to cut off Song relief troops.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve he defeated Sun Huchen at Dingjia Isle, then shifted to Huangchi to block Song reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 九月，從阿術與宋都統姜才戰，有功，加信武將軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he followed Aju to fight the Song commander-in-chief Jiang Cai, had merit, and was promoted to General of Trustworthy Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he fought under Aju against the Song commander Jiang Cai, distinguished himself, and was promoted to General of Trustworthy Martiality.

sentences.zh: 十三年，從下溫、台、福建。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he followed in reducing Wen, Tai, and Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirteen he helped subdue Wenzhou, Taizhou, and Fujian.

sentences.zh: 十四年，加懷遠大將軍、江陰路達魯花赤、水軍萬戶。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to Great General of Cherishing the Distant, darughachi of Jiangyin circuit, and naval ten-thousand-household.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen he was made Great General of Cherishing the Distant, darughachi of Jiangyin, and naval ten-thousand-household.

sentences.zh: 十六年，入朝，進昭勇大將軍、招討使。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he entered court and was advanced to Great General of Manifest Valor and pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In year sixteen he went to court and was promoted to Great General of Manifest Valor and pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十七年，加鎮國上將軍、都元帥。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to Suppressing-the-State Superior General and commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In year seventeen he was made Suppressing-the-State Superior General and commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷議徵日本，禧請行，即日拜行中書省平章政事，與右丞範文虎、左丞李庭同率舟師，泛海東征。

translations.literal: At that time the court was deliberating an expedition against Japan; Xi requested to go, and on the same day was appointed associate administrator of the Secretariat for the campaign, and together with the right vice premier Fan Wenhuge and left vice premier Li Ting led the fleet in a sea crossing to attack east.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated invading Japan, Xi volunteered and was appointed associate administrator of the Secretariat that same day. With Vice Premiers Fan Wenhuge and Li Ting he led the fleet across the sea.

sentences.zh: 至日本，禧即舍舟，築壘平湖島，約束戰艦，各相去五十步止泊，以避風濤觸擊。

translations.literal: On reaching Japan, Xi at once left the ships, built fortifications on Pinghu Isle, and regulated the warships so that each moored fifty paces apart to avoid wind and waves striking and colliding.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Japan, he went ashore on Pinghu Isle and built fortifications, spacing warships fifty paces apart so storms would not drive them together.

sentences.zh: 八月，颶風大作，文虎、庭戰艦悉壞，禧所部獨完。

translations.literal: In the eighth month a great typhoon arose; Wenhuge's and Ting's warships were all destroyed, while Xi's division alone remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month a typhoon wrecked Fan Wenhuge's and Li Ting's fleets; only Xi's squadron survived intact.

sentences.zh: 文虎等議還，禧曰：「士卒溺死者半，其脫死者，皆壯士也，曷若乘其無回顧心，因糧於敵以進戰。」

translations.literal: Wenhuge and others deliberated returning. Xi said: "Half the soldiers have drowned; those who escaped death are all stalwart men. Why not take advantage of their having no heart to look back, and live off the enemy's grain to advance and fight?"
translations.idiomatic: Fan Wenhuge and the others favored withdrawal. Xi said, "Half our men are drowned; the survivors are the hardiest troops. With no home to return to, why not forage from the enemy and press the attack?"

sentences.zh: 文虎等不從，曰：「還朝問罪，我輩當之，公不與也。」

translations.literal: Wenhuge and the others would not follow, saying: "If we return to court to answer for our crimes, we shall bear them; you will not be involved."
translations.idiomatic: They refused, saying, "If the court punishes us on our return, we will take the blame—you will not be implicated."

sentences.zh: 禧乃分船與之。

translations.literal: Xi then divided ships and gave them to them.
translations.idiomatic: Xi then gave them part of his fleet.

sentences.zh: 時平湖島屯兵四千，乏舟，禧曰：「我安忍棄之！」

translations.literal: At that time four thousand troops were garrisoned on Pinghu Isle and lacked boats. Xi said: "How can I bear to abandon them!"
translations.idiomatic: Four thousand men were stranded on Pinghu Isle without ships. Xi said, "How can I abandon them!"

sentences.zh: 遂悉棄舟中所有馬七十匹，以濟其還。

translations.literal: He then cast away all seventy horses in the boats to ferry their return.
translations.idiomatic: He threw overboard all seventy horses aboard his ships to make room for their evacuation.

sentences.zh: 至京師，文虎等皆獲罪，禧獨免。

translations.literal: On reaching the capital, Wenhuge and the others were all punished; Xi alone was exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital, Fan Wenhuge and the others were punished; Xi alone escaped censure.

sentences.zh: 子弘綱。

translations.literal: His son was Honggang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Honggang.

sentences.zh: 弘綱字憲臣，年十八，父禧為主將所誣，繫獄，將殺之，弘綱直入獄中，獄卒並系之。

translations.literal: Honggang, style Xianchen, at age eighteen—when his father Xi was falsely accused by the commanding general, imprisoned, and about to be executed—Honggang went straight into the prison; the jailers bound him as well.
translations.idiomatic: Honggang, styled Xianchen, was eighteen when his father was framed and jailed for execution. He walked into the prison; the guards seized him too.

sentences.zh: 弘綱佯狂謔笑，守者易之，既寢，遂與其父逸去。

translations.literal: Honggang feigned madness, jesting and laughing; the guards relaxed their vigilance. Once they had slept, he escaped with his father.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned madness, laughing and babbling until the guards grew careless. When they slept, father and son fled together.

sentences.zh: 後從其父攻城徇地，屢有功，自昭信校尉、管軍總把，佩銀符，換金符，為千戶，升總管、廣威將軍、招討副使，加定遠大將軍、招討使，襲鎮江陰。

translations.literal: Later he followed his father in storming cities and campaigning over territory, repeatedly having merit. He rose from Colonel of Manifest Trust and army commander, wore a silver tally, exchanged it for a gold tally, became chiliarch, was promoted to commander, General of Broad Prestige, and deputy pacification commissioner, was advanced to Great General of Fixing the Distant and pacification commissioner, and inherited command of Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: He later campaigned with his father, winning repeated honors—from Colonel of Manifest Trust and regimental commander with silver tally, then gold tally and chiliarch, to commander, General of Broad Prestige, deputy and then full pacification commissioner, and finally inherited the Jiangyin post.

sentences.zh: 盜起安吉，弘綱率兵往捕，未逾旬，擒之。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Anji; Honggang led troops to capture them and within less than ten days seized them.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Anji he led troops against them and captured the ringleaders in under ten days.

sentences.zh: 從參政高興破建德溪寨諸賊，後賜三珠虎符，授昭勇大將軍、河南諸翼徵行萬戶。

translations.literal: He followed the administrator Gao Xing in defeating the bandits of Jiande creek stockades and others; later he was granted a three-pearl tiger tally and appointed Great General of Manifest Valor and campaign ten-thousand-household of the various wings of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Administrator Gao Xing against the Jiande river-bandits and was later given a three-pearl tiger tally as Great General of Manifest Valor and campaign ten-thousand-household of Henan's wings.

sentences.zh: 從右丞劉深徵八百媳婦國，師次八番，與叛蠻宋隆濟等力戰而歿。

translations.literal: He followed the right vice premier Liu Shen on the expedition against the Kingdom of Eight Hundred Wives; the army halted in the Eight Fan regions and he died in fierce battle with the rebel barbarians Song Longji and others.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Vice Premier Liu Shen against the Kingdom of Eight Hundred Wives; the army halted in the Eight Fan country, and he fell fighting rebel tribesmen led by Song Longji.

sentences.zh: 贈宣忠秉義功臣、資善大夫、湖廣等處行中書省左丞、上護軍，追封齊郡公，諡武定。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title of merit noble who proclaims loyalty and upholds righteousness, Grand Master of Assisting in Goodness, left vice premier of the Huguang and other places Regional Secretariat, and Superior Guardian of the Army; was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Qi commandery, with the posthumous name Wuding.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as merit noble of proclaimed loyalty, Grand Master of Assisting in Goodness, left vice premier of the Huguang Secretariat, and Superior Guardian of the Army, enfeoffed as Duke of Qi with the posthumous name Wuding (Steadfast in War).

sentences.zh: 子漢，當襲職，讓其弟鼎。

translations.literal: His son Han was to inherit the office but yielded it to his younger brother Ding.
translations.idiomatic: His son Han was heir to the post but yielded it to his younger brother Ding.

sentences.zh: 漢後為監察御史，累官至集賢直學士。

translations.literal: Han later became investigating censor and rose through offices to Academician Direct of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Han later served as investigating censor and rose to Academician Direct of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 鼎，襲江陰水軍萬戶。

translations.literal: Ding inherited the post of naval ten-thousand-household of Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Ding inherited the Jiangyin naval ten-thousand-household post.

sentences.zh: 賈文備

translations.literal: Jia Wenbei
translations.idiomatic: Jia Wenbei

sentences.zh: 賈文備，字仲武，祁州蒲陰人。

translations.literal: Jia Wenbei, style Zhongwu, was a native of Puyin in Qi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Wenbei, styled Zhongwu, came from Puyin in Qi prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父輔，仕金為祁州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Fu served the Jin as prefect of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fu had served the Jin as prefect of Qi.

sentences.zh: 武仙憚輔膽略，密令所親圖之。

translations.literal: Wu Xian feared Fu's courage and stratagems and secretly ordered his intimates to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian feared Fu's boldness and cunning and secretly ordered his men to plot his downfall.

sentences.zh: 輔以眾歸太祖，詔隸張柔，以兵攻蠡州、慶都、安平、束鹿諸縣，皆下之。

translations.literal: Fu brought his followers to submit to Taizu; an edict placed him under Zhang Rou. With troops he attacked Li, Qingdu, Anping, Shulu, and other counties, and all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Fu defected with his troops to Genghis Khan and was assigned to Zhang Rou. He captured Li, Qingdu, Anping, Shulu, and neighboring counties.

sentences.zh: 柔開帥府於滿城，命輔行元帥府事於祁州。

translations.literal: Rou opened a marshal's headquarters at Mancheng and ordered Fu to conduct marshal's headquarters affairs at Qi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rou established headquarters at Mancheng and put Fu in charge of marshal's affairs at Qi.

sentences.zh: 從定山東，遷左副元帥。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Shandong and was transferred to left deputy marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He helped pacify Shandong and was made left deputy marshal.

sentences.zh: 柔將兵在外，輔常居守，累功改行軍千戶，賜金符，尋領順天河南等路軍民萬戶，卒。

translations.literal: When Rou led troops abroad, Fu regularly remained on guard. For accumulated merit he was changed to campaign chiliarch and granted a gold tally; soon he headed the Shuntian, Henan, and other circuits military-civilian ten-thousand-household, and died.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhang Rou campaigned abroad, Fu usually held the home front. For repeated service he became campaign chiliarch with a gold tally, then headed the Shuntian and Henan military-civilian ten-thousand-household before his death.

sentences.zh: 文備襲父千戶職，張柔命屯三汊口，備宋兵。

translations.literal: Wenbei inherited his father's chiliarch post; Zhang Rou ordered him to garrison at Sanchakou to guard against Song troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbei inherited his father's chiliarchcy; Zhang Rou stationed him at Sanchakou to watch the Song frontier.

sentences.zh: 宋以雲梯二十餘來攻，文備率兵鏖戰，卻之，憲宗賜弓矢銀盂。

translations.literal: Song came to attack with more than twenty siege ladders; Wenbei led troops in fierce battle and repelled them. Emperor Xianzong granted him bow and arrows and a silver bowl.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song attacked with more than twenty siege ladders, Wenbei fought them off. Emperor Möngke rewarded him with bow, arrows, and a silver bowl.

sentences.zh: 歲乙卯，復令襲父左副元帥職，兼領順天路。

translations.literal: In the year yimao he was again ordered to inherit his father's post as left deputy marshal and concurrently head Shuntian circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the yimao year (1255) he inherited his father's left deputy marshal post and took charge of Shuntian circuit.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，升開元府路女真水達達等處宣撫使，佩金虎府。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong he was promoted to pacification commissioner of Kaiyuan prefecture circuit, Jurchen, Shuidada, and other places, wearing a gold tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongtong 2 (1261) he was made pacification commissioner of Kaiyuan, the Jurchen and Shuidada territories, with a gold tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷開元東京懿州等處宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to pacification envoy of Kaiyuan, Eastern Capital, Yizhou, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he became pacification envoy of Kaiyuan, Eastern Capital, Yizhou, and neighboring regions.

sentences.zh: 四年，改授萬戶，領張柔所部軍，屯亳州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was reassigned as ten-thousand-household, commanding Zhang Rou's former troops, garrisoned at Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he was made ten-thousand-household over Zhang Rou's old command and garrisoned at Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 宋兵時鈔掠淮甸，文備戰卻之。

translations.literal: Song troops often raided and plundered the Huai region; Wenbei fought and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly drove off Song raiders in the Huai region.

sentences.zh: 至元二年，加昭勇大將軍、真定路總管，兼府尹。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan he was promoted to Great General of Manifest Valor and commander of Zhending circuit, concurrently serving as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 2 (1265) he was made Great General of Manifest Valor and commander-prefect of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 六年，調衛輝路總管​​。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to commander of Weihui circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he was transferred to commander of Weihui.

sentences.zh: 七年，授西蜀成都統軍，以疾不赴。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed commander-in-chief of Chengdu in Western Shu, but because of illness did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven he was named commander-in-chief at Chengdu in western Shu but declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 八年，授宿州萬戶，尋改河南等路統軍，圍襄樊。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed ten-thousand-household of Suzhou; soon he was changed to commander-in-chief of Henan and other circuits and besieged Xiangyang and Fancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight he was made ten-thousand-household of Suzhou, then commander-in-chief of Henan and joined the siege of Xiangyang and Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 九年，移蔡州，兼水陸漕運。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was moved to Caizhou, concurrently in charge of water and land grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine he was posted to Caizhou with charge of river and land grain transport.

sentences.zh: 宋兵時掠糧餉，文備敗之，並奪其船。

translations.literal: Song troops often plundered grain supplies; Wenbei defeated them and also seized their boats.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Song forces raiding supply lines and seized their boats.

sentences.zh: 詔罷統軍，文備入覲，賜弓矢、金鞍、錦衣、白金。

translations.literal: An edict dismissed him from commander-in-chief; Wenbei entered court for an audience and was granted bow and arrows, a gold saddle, brocade robes, and white gold.
translations.idiomatic: When the commander-in-chief post was abolished he went to court and received bow, arrows, a gold saddle, brocade robes, and silver.

sentences.zh: 十一年，复授萬戶、漢軍都元帥，領劉整軍，駐亳州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was again appointed ten-thousand-household and commander-in-chief of Han armies, commanding Liu Zheng's army, garrisoned at Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven he was again made ten-thousand-household and Han-army commander-in-chief over Liu Zheng's forces at Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 宋將夏貴知亳無備，盛引兵來襲，文備出奇邀擊，大破之，帝賜金鞍、金織、文段、白金。

translations.literal: The Song general Xia Gui, knowing Bozhou was unprepared, led a large force in a surprise attack. Wenbei struck with an unexpected ambush and routed them greatly; the Emperor granted a gold saddle, gold brocade, patterned silks, and white gold.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Bozhou was undefended, Xia Gui launched a major raid. Wenbei ambushed and routed him; the Emperor rewarded him with a gold saddle, brocade, patterned silks, and silver.

sentences.zh: 丞相伯顏伐宋，文備領左翼諸軍以從，抵郢州。

translations.literal: When Chancellor Bayan attacked Song, Wenbei led the various armies of the left wing in following and reached Ying prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Bayan invaded Song, Wenbei led the left wing to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 宋築二城夾江，布戰艦數千艘於江中，陳兵兩岸，軍不得進。

translations.literal: Song built two cities flanking the river, deployed several thousand warships in the river, and arrayed troops on both banks; the army could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The Song had twin cities on the river, thousands of warships in the channel, and troops on both banks—the army could not advance.

sentences.zh: 文備泛舟，由淪河徑出大江，攻武磯堡。

translations.literal: Wenbei floated boats, went by the Lun River straight out to the Great River, and attacked Wuji fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbei took boats up the Lun River into the Yangzi and assaulted Wuji fortress.

sentences.zh: 乃從阿術先渡江，大軍繼之，遂取鄂、漢，以功賜白金，加昭毅大將軍，守鄂州。

translations.literal: He then followed Aju in crossing the river first; the great army followed, and thus took E and Han. For merit he was granted white gold, promoted to Great General of Manifest Resolution, and left to guard Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed first with Aju; the main army followed and took Ezhou and Hankou. For this he received silver, was made Great General of Manifest Resolution, and garrisoned Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 十二年，從平章政事阿里海牙趣湖南，至潭州城下。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he followed the associate administrator Alai Haiya in pressing Hunan and reached below the walls of Tan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve he marched into Hunan under Associate Administrator Alai Haiya and reached Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 文備冒鋒鏑，砲傷右手，流矢中左臂，攻戰愈急，宋臣李芾死之，轉運判官鐘蜚英等以城降。

translations.literal: Wenbei braved blades and arrows; a cannon wounded his right hand and a stray arrow struck his left arm. The attack grew fiercer; the Song minister Li Fei died, and the transport vice commissioner Zhong Feiying and others surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbei fought in the front rank; a cannon ball wounded his right hand and an arrow his left arm. The assault intensified until the Song minister Li Fei died and Transport Vice Commissioner Zhong Feiying surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 十三年，加昭武大將軍，守潭州。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to Great General of Manifest Martiality and guarded Tan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirteen he was promoted to Great General of Manifest Martiality and left to guard Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 十四年，衡、永、郴等郡寇發，文備悉討平之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year bandits rose in Heng, Yong, Chen, and other prefectures; Wenbei pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen he suppressed rebellions in Heng, Yong, Chen, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 十五年，進鎮國上將軍、湖南道宣慰使，徇瓊崖等州及廣東瀕海諸城，追宋衛王昺。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was advanced to Suppressing-the-State Superior General and pacification envoy of Hunan circuit, campaigning through Qiongya and other prefectures and the coastal cities of Guangdong, pursuing the Song Prince Wei Zhao Bing.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifteen he was made Suppressing-the-State Superior General and Hunan pacification envoy, campaigning through Hainan and Guangdong's coastal cities in pursuit of the Song prince Zhao Bing.

sentences.zh: 十六年，召還，拜淮東宣慰使，加金吾上將軍，鎮慶元。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was recalled, appointed pacification envoy of Huaidong, promoted to Golden Guard Superior General, and garrisoned Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In year sixteen he was recalled, made Huaidong pacification envoy and Golden Guard Superior General, and stationed at Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 十八年，复授都元帥。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was again appointed commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In year eighteen he was again made commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 二十年，改江東宣慰使，討建寧盜黃華。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was changed to pacification envoy of Jiangdong and suppressed the Jianning bandit Huang Hua.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty he became Jiangdong pacification envoy and suppressed the Jianning rebel Huang Hua.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，拜荊湖占城行中書省參知政事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was appointed associate administrator of the Jinghu-Champa Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-two he was made associate administrator of the Jinghu-Champa Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，改湖廣行省參知政事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was transferred to associate administrator of the Huguang Regional Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-three he was transferred to associate administrator of the Huguang Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，致仕。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-four he retired from office.

sentences.zh: 後十七年，以疾卒。

translations.literal: Seventeen years later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeen years later he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 延祐四年，贈江西等處行中書省左丞，追封武威郡公，諡莊武。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yanyou he was posthumously granted left vice premier of the Jiangxi and other places Regional Secretariat, posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Wuwei commandery, with the posthumous name Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 4 he was posthumously made left vice premier of the Jiangxi Secretariat, enfeoffed as Duke of Wuwei, with the posthumous name Zhuangwu (Solemn in War).

sentences.zh: ○解誠

translations.literal: Xie Cheng
translations.idiomatic: Xie Cheng

sentences.zh: 解誠，易州定興人，善水戰，從伐宋，設方略，奪敵船千計，以功授金符、水軍萬戶，兼都水監使。

translations.literal: Xie Cheng was a native of Dingxing in Yi prefecture, skilled in naval warfare. He followed the attack on Song, devised stratagems, and seized enemy ships by the thousands. For merit he was granted a gold tally, appointed naval ten-thousand-household, and concurrently superintendent of the Directorate of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Cheng of Dingxing in Yi prefecture excelled at naval combat. Campaigning against Song he devised tactics and captured thousands of enemy vessels, earning a gold tally, the naval ten-thousand-household post, and the waterways superintendency.

sentences.zh: 焦湖之戰，獲戰艦三百艘。

translations.literal: In the battle of Jiao Lake he captured three hundred warships.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiao Lake he captured three hundred warships.

sentences.zh: 宋以舟師來援，誠據舟厲聲呵之，援兵不敢動，急移舟抵岸，乘勢追殺之，奪其軍餉三百餘斛。

translations.literal: Song sent a fleet to relieve the city; Cheng stood on his boat and shouted them down in a fierce voice. The relief troops dared not move, hurriedly shifted boats to shore, and he seized the moment to pursue and kill them, seizing more than three hundred hu of their military grain.
translations.idiomatic: When Song sent a relief fleet, Cheng stood in his boat and roared them down until they froze, then rushed ashore in pursuit and seized over three hundred hu of military grain.

sentences.zh: 既又從攻安豐、壽、复、泗、亳諸州，俱有功。

translations.literal: He again followed attacks on Anfeng, Shou, Fu, Si, and Bo prefectures, and in all had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He later fought at Anfeng, Shou, Fu, Si, and Bo and distinguished himself in each.

sentences.zh: 又從下雲南大理國，以功賜金虎符。

translations.literal: He again followed in reducing Yunnan and the Dali kingdom; for merit he was granted a gold tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the conquest of Yunnan and Dali and received a gold tiger tally for his service.

sentences.zh: 從攻鄂，奪敵艦千餘艘，殺溺敵軍甚眾。

translations.literal: He followed the attack on Ezhou, seized more than a thousand enemy vessels, and killed or drowned very many enemy troops.
translations.idiomatic: At the assault on Ezhou he captured over a thousand enemy ships and killed or drowned a great many Song troops.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘉其功，嘗降制獎之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu praised his achievements and once issued an imperial rescript to reward him.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai Khan praised his achievements and once issued an imperial rescript commending him.

sentences.zh: 至元三十年，卒，贈推忠宣力功臣、龍虎衛上將軍、同知樞密院事、上護軍，追封易國公，諡武定。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Zhiyuan he died. He was posthumously granted the title of merit noble who promotes loyalty and displays strength, Superior General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard, associate administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and Superior Guardian of the Army; was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yi state, with the posthumous name Wuding.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhiyuan 30, posthumously honored as merit noble of loyalty and strength, Superior General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard, associate administrator of military affairs, and Superior Guardian of the Army, enfeoffed as Duke of Yi with the posthumous name Wuding.

sentences.zh: 子汝楫襲，從討李璮，平宋，累獲功賞，卒，贈推忠效節功臣、資德大夫、中書右丞、上護軍，追封易國公，諡忠毅。

translations.literal: His son Ruji inherited the post, followed in suppressing Li Tan and pacifying Song, repeatedly received merit rewards, and died. He was posthumously granted the title of merit noble who promotes loyalty and displays integrity, Grand Master of Assisting in Virtue, right vice premier of the Secretariat, and Superior Guardian of the Army; was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yi state, with the posthumous name Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ruji inherited the post, fought Li Tan and helped conquer Song, and won repeated honors before his death. He was posthumously made merit noble of loyal service, Grand Master of Assisting in Virtue, right vice premier, and Superior Guardian of the Army, enfeoffed as Duke of Yi with the posthumous name Zhongyi.

sentences.zh: 子帖哥襲，從征廣西，下靜江府，改授水軍招討使。

translations.literal: His son Tiege inherited; he followed the campaign in Guangxi, took Jingjiang prefecture, and was reassigned as naval pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tiege inherited, campaigned in Guangxi, captured Jingjiang, and was made naval pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 尋復為萬戶，從征交趾，有功，升廣東道宣慰使，卒，贈資德大夫、河南江北等處行中書省左丞、上護軍、平陽郡公，諡武宣。

translations.literal: Soon he was again made ten-thousand-household; he followed the campaign against Jiaozhi, had merit, and was promoted to pacification envoy of Guangdong circuit. He died and was posthumously granted Grand Master of Assisting in Virtue, left vice premier of the Henan, Jiangbei, and other places Regional Secretariat, Superior Guardian of the Army, and Duke of Pingyang commandery, with the posthumous name Wuxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon restored as ten-thousand-household, he campaigned in Jiaozhi with distinction and became Guangdong pacification envoy. After his death he was honored as Grand Master of Assisting in Virtue, left vice premier of the Henan and Jiangbei Secretariat, Superior Guardian of the Army, and Duke of Pingyang, posthumous name Wuxuan.

sentences.zh: 子世英，由監察御史遷山南江北道僉事。

translations.literal: His son Shiying rose from investigating censor to commissioner of the Shannan-Jiangbei circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiying rose from investigating censor to commissioner of the Shannan-Jiangbei circuit.

sentences.zh: ○管如德

translations.literal: Guan Rude
translations.idiomatic: Guan Rude

sentences.zh: 管如德，黃州黃陂縣人。

translations.literal: Guan Rude was a native of Huangpi county in Huang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Rude came from Huangpi in Huang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父景模，為宋將，以蘄州降，授淮西宣撫使。

translations.literal: His father Jingmo was a Song general who surrendered with Qizhou and was appointed pacification commissioner of Huai west.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingmo, a Song general, surrendered Qizhou and was made Huai west pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 如德為江州都統制，至元十二年，亦以城降。

translations.literal: Rude was commander-in-chief of Jiang prefecture; in the twelfth year of Zhiyuan he too surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Rude was Jiangzhou commander-in-chief; in Zhiyuan 12 he too surrendered his city.

sentences.zh: 先是，如德嘗被俘虜，思其父，與同輩七人間道南馳，為邏者所獲，械送於郡。

translations.literal: Earlier Rude had once been taken captive. Longing for his father, he and seven companions of his age fled south by hidden paths; they were seized by scouts, shackled, and sent to the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier he had been captured. Yearning for his father, he and seven companions fled south by back roads, were seized by scouts, shackled, and sent to the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 如德伺邏者怠，即引械擊死數十人，各破械脫走，間關萬里達父所。

translations.literal: Rude watched until the scouts grew slack, then used his shackles to strike and kill several dozen men; each broke his bonds and escaped, and after hardships over ten thousand li he reached his father's place.
translations.idiomatic: When the guards relaxed, he used his shackles to kill dozens of them; all broke free and, after a perilous journey of ten thousand li, reached his father.

sentences.zh: 景模喜曰：「此真吾兒也！」

translations.literal: Jingmo said in joy: "This is truly my son!"
translations.idiomatic: Jingmo exclaimed in delight, "This is truly my son!"

sentences.zh: 至是，入覲，世祖笑曰：「是孝於父者，必忠於我矣。」

translations.literal: At this time he entered court for an audience. Emperor Shizu smiled and said: "One who is filial to his father will surely be loyal to me."
translations.idiomatic: When he came to court, Kublai smiled and said, "A man so filial to his father will surely be loyal to me."

sentences.zh: 一日，授以強弓二，如德以左手兼握，右手悉引滿之，帝曰：「得無傷汝臂乎？

translations.literal: One day he was given two powerful bows. Rude grasped both with his left hand and fully drew them all with his right. The Emperor said: "Will this not injure your arm?
translations.idiomatic: One day the Emperor gave him two powerful bows. Rude gripped both with his left hand and drew each to the full with his right. The Khan asked, "Won't that injure your arm?

sentences.zh: 後毋复然！」

translations.literal: Hereafter do not do so again!"
translations.idiomatic: Don't do that again!"

sentences.zh: 嘗從獵，遇大溝，馬不可越，如德即解衣浮渡，帝壯之，由是稱為拔都，賞賚優渥。

translations.literal: Once when following a hunt they came to a great ditch that horses could not cross; Rude at once stripped and swam across. The Emperor admired his strength and from this called him Batu, rewarding him generously.
translations.idiomatic: On a hunt they came to a ditch horses could not cross; Rude stripped and swam it. The Khan admired his strength, called him Batu, and rewarded him generously.

sentences.zh: 帝問：「我何以得天下，宋何以亡？」

translations.literal: The Emperor asked: "How did I obtain the empire, and how did Song perish?"
translations.idiomatic: The Khan asked, "How did I win the empire, and why did Song fall?"

sentences.zh: 如德對曰：「陛下以福德勝之。

translations.literal: Rude replied: "Your Majesty overcame them by virtue and fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Rude answered, "Your Majesty prevailed through virtue and fortune.

sentences.zh: 襄樊，宋咽喉也，咽喉被塞，不亡何恃！」

translations.literal: Xiangyang and Fancheng were Song's throat; when the throat is blocked, on what can they rely not to perish!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang and Fancheng were Song's throat—once that throat was choked, how could they survive!"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Well said."
translations.idiomatic: The Khan said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 帝又命習國書，曰：「習成，當為朕言之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor also ordered him to study the national script, saying: "When you have mastered it, you shall speak to me in it."
translations.idiomatic: The Khan ordered him to learn Mongolian script, saying, "When you have mastered it, speak to me in it."

sentences.zh: 一日，帝語如德曰：「朕治天下，重惜人命，凡有罪者必令面對再四，果實也而後罪之，非如宋權奸擅權，書片紙數字即殺人也。

translations.literal: One day the Emperor said to Rude: "In governing the empire I greatly cherish human life. For all who have guilt I always have them confronted face to face again and again; only when it is verified do I punish them—not like Song's powerful traitors who monopolized authority and killed people on a slip of paper with a few characters.
translations.idiomatic: One day the Khan told him, "I cherish human life in governing the realm. The guilty are questioned face to face again and again, and only when guilt is proved are they punished—not like Song's powerful ministers who killed men on a scrap of paper with a few characters.

sentences.zh: 汝但一心奉職，毋懼忌嫉之口。」

translations.literal: You need only devote yourself wholeheartedly to your duties; do not fear mouths of envy and jealousy."
translations.idiomatic: Serve faithfully and do not fear the envious."

sentences.zh: 授湖北招討使，總管本部軍馬，佩金虎符。

translations.literal: He was appointed pacification commissioner of Hubei, commander-in-chief of his original command's troops and horses, wearing a gold tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Hubei pacification commissioner, commander of his original forces, with a gold tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 是年六月，丞相阿術南攻宋。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of that year Chancellor Aju attacked Song in the south.
translations.idiomatic: That sixth month Chancellor Aju invaded Song from the south.

sentences.zh: 如德以軍為前鋒，至揚州揚子橋，與宋戰，晝夜不息，如德先登陷陣，擒其帥張都統等，宋軍遂潰。

translations.literal: Rude led the army as vanguard to Yangzi Bridge at Yang prefecture and fought Song; day and night without cease. Rude was first to ascend and break the formation, capturing their commander Commander Zhang and others; Song troops then collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Rude led the vanguard to Yangzi Bridge at Yangzhou and fought day and night without rest. He was first over the wall, captured Commander Zhang and others, and routed the Song army.

sentences.zh: 七月，進軍焦山江上，復大戰，奪宋帥夏都統牌印衣甲及餉軍海船，悉送阿術所。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the army advanced to the Jiaoshan river line and fought another great battle, seizing Commander Xia's tally, seals, armor, and supply ships, all sent to Aju's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month they fought again on the Jiaoshan river, seizing Commander Xia's tally, seals, armor, and supply fleet, all sent to Aju.

sentences.zh: 事聞，帝命賞之。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the Emperor ordered him rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered him rewarded when he heard.

sentences.zh: 軍至鎮江，如德招安諸郡，守將皆望風降附。

translations.literal: When the army reached Zhenjiang, Rude pacified and reassured the various prefectures; defending generals all surrendered at the sight of his banners.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhenjiang he pacified the surrounding prefectures; garrison commanders surrendered at the sight of his banners.

sentences.zh: 丞相伯顏取臨安，復選能招諸郡者，眾推如德，如德銜命往喻，紹興諸郡皆下。

translations.literal: When Chancellor Bayan took Lin'an, he again selected those able to win over the prefectures; all recommended Rude. Rude received the commission and went to persuade them; Shaoxing and the other prefectures all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Bayan took Lin'an he chose men to win over the prefectures; all named Rude, who went on imperial commission and brought Shaoxing and the rest to submit.

sentences.zh: 初，世祖以寶刀賜如德，及與敵戰，刀刃盡缺。

translations.literal: Earlier Emperor Shizu had granted Rude a precious saber; in fighting the enemy the blade was entirely nicked.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai had once given him a fine saber; in battle its edge was chipped throughout.

sentences.zh: 宋平，入覲，如德以刀上呈，曰：「陛下向所賜刀，從軍以來，刀缺如是矣。」

translations.literal: When Song was pacified he entered court for an audience. Rude presented the saber and said: "Your Majesty's saber once granted—since joining the army, the blade is nicked thus."
translations.idiomatic: After Song fell he came to court and presented the saber, saying, "The blade Your Majesty once gave is nicked like this from campaigning."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其樸。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his plain honesty.
translations.idiomatic: The Khan praised his plain honesty.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遷浙西宣慰使，上時政五條：一曰立額薄徵；

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to pacification envoy of western Zhejiang and submitted five items on current policy: first, set quotas and levy lightly;
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve he became western Zhejiang pacification envoy and submitted five policy proposals: first, set tax quotas and levy lightly;

sentences.zh: 二曰息兵懷遠；

translations.literal: second, cease warfare and cherish the distant;
translations.idiomatic: second, cease warfare and cherish distant peoples;

sentences.zh: 三曰立法用人；

translations.literal: third, establish laws and employ men;
translations.idiomatic: third, establish laws and appoint worthy men;

sentences.zh: 四曰省役恤民；

translations.literal: fourth, reduce corvée labor and show compassion to the people;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, reduce corvée and show compassion to the people;

sentences.zh: 五曰設官制祿。

translations.literal: fifth, establish offices and fix salaries.
translations.idiomatic: fifth, establish offices and fix official salaries.

sentences.zh: 時法制未備，仕多冗員，又方用兵日本倭國，而軍民之官，廩祿未有定制，故如德言及之。

translations.literal: At that time the legal system was not yet complete, offices had many redundant appointees, and troops were being deployed against Japan; yet salaries for military and civilian officials had no fixed regulation—therefore Rude spoke of these matters.
translations.idiomatic: Institutions were still incomplete, offices were overstaffed, and war with Japan was underway, yet military and civilian salaries had no fixed scale—hence Rude raised these points.

sentences.zh: 權臣抑不得上。

translations.literal: Powerful ministers suppressed the memorial and it could not reach the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful ministers blocked the memorial from reaching the throne.

sentences.zh: 二十年，丞相阿塔海命馳驛奏出征事，入見，世祖問曰：「江南之民，得無有二心乎？」

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Chancellor Atahai ordered him to ride post-horses to memorialize on the expedition. On entering audience Emperor Shizu asked: "Can the people of Jiangnan be without divided hearts?"
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty Chancellor Atahai sent him by post relay to report on the expedition. At audience Kublai asked, "Can the people of Jiangnan still harbor disloyalty?"

sentences.zh: 如德對曰：「往歲旱澇相仍，民不聊生，今累歲豐稔，民沐聖恩多矣，敢有貳志！

translations.literal: Rude replied: "In former years drought and flood followed one another and the people could barely live. Now for successive years harvests have been abundant; the people have bathed in sagely grace—how would they dare harbor divided hearts!
translations.idiomatic: Rude answered, "In past years drought and flood followed one another and the people could barely survive. Now harvests have been abundant for years and they have bathed in Your Majesty's grace—how could they harbor disloyalty!

sentences.zh: 使果有貳志，臣曷敢飾辭以欺陛下乎！」

translations.literal: If they truly had divided hearts, how would your servant dare embellish his words to deceive Your Majesty!"
translations.idiomatic: If they truly were disloyal, how would I dare deceive Your Majesty with fine words!"

sentences.zh: 帝善其言，且喻之曰：「阿塔海有未及者，卿善輔導之，有當奏聞者，卿勿憚勞，宜馳捷足之馬，來告於朕。」

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his words and also instructed him: "Where Atahai falls short, you should guide him well. Where there is matter that should be reported, do not shrink from labor—ride a swift horse and come tell me."
translations.idiomatic: The Khan approved and added, "Where Atahai falls short, guide him. When something must be reported, spare no effort—ride a swift horse and tell me."

sentences.zh: 二十四年，遷江西行省參知政事，破豪猾，去姦吏，居民大悅。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to associate administrator of the Jiangxi Regional Secretariat, broke powerful ruffians, removed corrupt officials, and the residents were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-four he became associate administrator of the Jiangxi Secretariat, broke powerful ruffians, removed corrupt officials, and won the people's gratitude.

sentences.zh: 是時贛、汀二州盜起，如德指揮諸將討平之，其脅從者多所全宥。

translations.literal: At that time bandits rose in Gan and Ting prefectures; Rude directed the generals to suppress and pacify them, and many of those coerced to follow were fully pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Gan and Ting he directed the generals to suppress them and pardoned many who had been coerced.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，遷江西行尚書省左丞，時鐘明亮以循州叛，殺掠州縣，千里丘墟，帝命如德統四省兵討之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was transferred to left vice premier of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat. At that time Zhong Mingliang rebelled with Xun prefecture, killing and plundering prefectures and counties until a thousand li were wasteland; the Emperor ordered Rude to command troops of four provinces to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-six he became left vice premier of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat. Zhong Mingliang rebelled from Xunzhou, ravaging the region for a thousand li; the Emperor ordered Rude to command troops from four provinces against him.

sentences.zh: 諸將欲直搗其巢穴，如德曰：「嘻！

translations.literal: The generals wished to strike straight at his lair. Rude said: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: The generals wanted to strike his stronghold directly. Rude said, "Alas!

sentences.zh: 今田野之氓，疲於轉輸，介冑之士，病於暴露，重困斯民，而自為功，吾不為也。」

translations.literal: Now the rustics of field and plain are weary from transport labor, and armored warriors are afflicted by exposure. To redouble hardship on these people while seeking merit for myself—I will not do it."
translations.idiomatic: The farmers are worn out hauling supplies and the soldiers are worn by exposure. I will not heap more suffering on the people just to win glory for myself."

sentences.zh: 於是遣使喻以禍福，賊感如德誠信，即擁十餘騎詣贛州石城縣降。

translations.literal: He then sent envoys to explain fortune and calamity; the bandits were moved by Rude's sincerity and trustworthiness and at once led a dozen or so horsemen to Shicheng county in Gan prefecture to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to explain the consequences; moved by his sincerity, the rebels came with a dozen horsemen to surrender at Shicheng in Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 平章政事奧魯赤怒其跋扈不臣，欲以事殺明亮，如德聞之曰：「皇元仁厚，未嘗殺降，明亮叛人，何足惜，所重者，信不可失耳！」

translations.literal: Associate Administrator Oluchi was angry at his overbearing disloyalty and wished to find cause to kill Mingliang. Hearing this, Rude said: "The Yuan is benevolent and generous and has never killed those who surrender. Mingliang is a rebel—what is there to regret? What matters is that trust must not be lost!"
translations.idiomatic: Associate Administrator Oluchi, angered by Mingliang's arrogance, wished to kill him. Rude said, "The Yuan is benevolent and has never killed those who surrender. Mingliang is a rebel of little account; what matters is that we must not break faith."

sentences.zh: 年四十有四，卒於軍，贈江西行省左丞、平昌郡公，諡武襄。

translations.literal: At age forty-four he died in the army. He was posthumously granted left vice premier of the Jiangxi Regional Secretariat and Duke of Pingchang commandery, with the posthumous name Wuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in camp at forty-four, posthumously honored as left vice premier of Jiangxi and Duke of Pingchang, posthumous name Wuxiang.

sentences.zh: 子九，淳祖，積官中順大夫、龍興路富州尹。

translations.literal: He had nine sons; Chunzu rose through offices to Grand Master of Central Compliance and prefect of Fuzhou in Longxing circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He had nine sons; Chunzu rose to Grand Master of Central Compliance and prefect of Fuzhou in Longxing circuit.

sentences.zh: ○趙匣剌

translations.literal: Zhao Xiala
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xiala

sentences.zh: 趙匣剌者，始以父任為千戶，佩金符。

translations.literal: Zhao Xiala at first held the chiliarch post through his father's appointment and wore a gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xiala first held a chiliarch post by his father's appointment, with a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 中統三年，守東川。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong he guarded Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongtong 3 he garrisoned Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 四年，宋夏貴以兵侵虎嘯山寨，元帥飲察遣匣剌率兵往御之，貴敗走，追至新明縣，斬首三十餘級。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Song general Xia Gui invaded Huxiao Mountain stockade with troops. Marshal Yinchai sent Xiala to lead troops to resist; Gui was defeated and fled. Pursuit reached Xinming county and more than thirty heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: In year four Xia Gui attacked Huxiao Mountain stockade. Marshal Yinchai sent Xiala to repel him; Gui fled and was pursued to Xinming, where over thirty heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 宋劉雄飛以兵犯青居山舊府，匣剌與戰於都尉壩，敗之，斬首二十餘級。

translations.literal: The Song general Liu Xiongfei invaded the old prefectural seat at Qingju Mountain with troops. Xiala fought him at Duyu Dam, defeated him, and took more than twenty heads.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiongfei attacked the old Qingju Mountain seat; Xiala defeated him at Duyu Dam and took over twenty heads.

sentences.zh: 欽察攻釣魚山，遣匣剌以兵千五百人略地至南壩，擊敗宋軍，生獲軍士五十七人，老幼三百四十人。

translations.literal: Qinchai attacked Diaoyu Mountain and sent Xiala with fifteen hundred troops to raid as far as Nanba, defeating Song troops and capturing alive fifty-seven soldiers and three hundred forty old and young.
translations.idiomatic: Qinchai attacked Diaoyu Mountain and sent Xiala with fifteen hundred men to raid to Nanba, defeating Song forces and capturing fifty-seven soldiers and three hundred forty civilians.

sentences.zh: 從攻大良平，宋昝萬壽運糧至渠江之鵝灘，匣剌邀擊之，斬首五十餘級，宋兵大敗。

translations.literal: He followed the attack on Daliangping. Song's Zan Wanshou transported grain to Etan on the Qu River; Xiala intercepted and struck them, taking more than fifty heads, and Song troops were greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: At Daliangping he intercepted Zan Wanshou's grain convoy at Etan on the Qu River, took over fifty heads, and routed the Song army.

sentences.zh: 匣剌亦被三創，矢鏃中左肩不得出。

translations.literal: Xiala also received three wounds; an arrowhead struck his left shoulder and could not be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiala took three wounds; an arrowhead lodged in his left shoulder and could not be extracted.

sentences.zh: 欽察惜其驍勇，取死囚二人，刲其肩，視骨節淺深，知可出，即為鑿其創，拔鏃出之，匣剌神色不為動。

translations.literal: Qinchai prized his valor; he took two condemned prisoners, cut open their shoulders, observed the depth of bone and joint, knew the arrowhead could be removed, then bored Xiala's wound and drew out the arrowhead. Xiala's expression did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Qinchai, valuing his bravery, had two condemned men cut open so he could gauge the wound depth, then bored Xiala's shoulder and extracted the arrowhead while Xiala's expression never changed.

sentences.zh: 至元三年，為東川路先鋒使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhiyuan he was made vanguard commissioner of Dongchuan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 3 he was made Dongchuan vanguard commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四年，元帥拜答攻開州，至萬寶山，遣匣剌以兵五百人擊宋軍，生獲四十人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Marshal Baida attacked Kaizhou and reached Wanbao Mountain; he sent Xiala with five hundred troops to strike Song troops and captured forty alive.
translations.idiomatic: In year four Marshal Baida attacked Kaizhou and sent Xiala with five hundred men against Song forces, capturing forty alive.

sentences.zh: 五年，兼管京兆、延安兩路新軍，戍東安、虎嘯山兩城。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he concurrently commanded the new armies of Jingzhao and Yan'an circuits and garrisoned the two cities of Dong'an and Huxiao Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he commanded new forces of Jingzhao and Yan'an and garrisoned Dong'an and Huxiao Mountain.

sentences.zh: 宋楊立以兵護糧，送大良平，匣剌察知之，遂率所部兵與立戰於三重山，斬首百五十級，擒獲四十餘人。

translations.literal: Song's Yang Li escorted grain with troops to Daliangping. Xiala detected this and led his command to fight Li at Triple Mountain, taking one hundred fifty heads and capturing more than forty men.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Li escorted grain to Daliangping; Xiala detected it and fought him at Triple Mountain, taking one hundred fifty heads and over forty prisoners.

sentences.zh: 立敗走，棄其糧千餘石，因盡奪其甲仗旗幟而還。

translations.literal: Li was defeated and fled, abandoning more than a thousand shi of grain; Xiala then seized all their armor, weapons, banners, and flags and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Li fled, abandoning over a thousand shi of grain; Xiala seized all their arms, armor, and banners and returned.

sentences.zh: 六年，行院遣匣剌攻釣魚山之沙市，焚其敵樓。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the campaign headquarters sent Xiala to attack Shashi at Diaoyu Mountain and burned its watchtowers.
translations.idiomatic: In year six headquarters sent him against Shashi at Diaoyu Mountain, where he burned the watchtowers.

sentences.zh: 從左丞曲力吉思等入朝，詔賞白金五十兩，細甲一注。

translations.literal: He followed the left vice premier Qulijisi and others to court; an edict rewarded him with fifty liang of white gold and one suit of fine armor.
translations.idiomatic: He went to court with Left Vice Premier Qulijisi and was rewarded with fifty liang of silver and a suit of fine armor.

sentences.zh: 九年，統軍合剌攻釣魚山，時匣剌為先鋒，領兵千人，略地至葛樹坪，與宋兵遇，生獲二十餘人，斬首四十級。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Commander Hela attacked Diaoyu Mountain; Xiala was then vanguard, leading a thousand troops to raid as far as Geshu Plain. Meeting Song troops he captured more than twenty alive and took forty heads.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine Commander Hela attacked Diaoyu Mountain with Xiala as vanguard; at Geshu Plain he captured over twenty alive and took forty heads.

sentences.zh: 十年三月，復從行院合答攻釣魚山之沙市，匣剌乘夜蟻附而登，殺其守兵，燒其積聚，生獲二十餘人以歸。

translations.literal: In the third month of the tenth year he again followed headquarters commander Heda to attack Shashi at Diaoyu Mountain. Xiala scaled the wall by night like ants climbing, killed the garrison troops, burned their stores, and returned with more than twenty captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year ten he scaled Shashi at Diaoyu Mountain by night, killed the garrison, burned the stores, and returned with over twenty captives.

sentences.zh: 又擊敗宋將張珏兵於武勝軍。

translations.literal: He again defeated the troops of the Song general Zhang Yu at Wusheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: He also defeated Song general Zhang Yu at Wusheng.

sentences.zh: 行院新拔禮義山寨，命匣剌守之。

translations.literal: Headquarters had newly taken Liyi Mountain stockade and ordered Xiala to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: When headquarters took Liyi Mountain stockade, Xiala was ordered to hold it.

sentences.zh: 十二年，率舟師會攻釣魚山，戰數有功。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he led the fleet in a joint attack on Diaoyu Mountain and repeatedly had merit in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve he led the fleet in the joint assault on Diaoyu Mountain with repeated distinction.

sentences.zh: 進圍重慶，宋將趙安勒兵出戰，匣剌迎擊之，夜至二鼓，敵眾大潰。

translations.literal: Advancing to besiege Chongqing, the Song general Zhao An led troops out to fight; Xiala met and struck them. By the second watch of the night the enemy host was greatly routed.
translations.idiomatic: Besieging Chongqing, he met Zhao An's sortie and routed the enemy by the second watch of the night.

sentences.zh: 行院以其功上聞，未報而疾作，乃遣往瀘州治疾。

translations.literal: Headquarters reported his merit upward; before a reply came illness seized him, and he was sent to Luzhou to treat the illness.
translations.idiomatic: Headquarters reported his merit, but before a reply came he fell ill and was sent to Luzhou for treatment.

sentences.zh: 至之夕，瀘州复叛，匣剌輿疾出戰，遂為其所獲，與從者二十人皆死之。

translations.literal: On the evening he arrived Luzhou rebelled again. Xiala went out to fight despite his illness in a litter and was captured by them; he and twenty followers all died.
translations.idiomatic: The night he arrived Luzhou rebelled again. He went out to fight despite his illness and was captured; he and twenty followers all died.

sentences.zh: 子世顯，船橋副萬戶。

translations.literal: His son Shixian was deputy ten-thousand-household of the boat bridge.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shixian was deputy ten-thousand-household of the boat bridge.

sentences.zh: ○周全

translations.literal: Zhou Quan
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Quan

sentences.zh: 周全，其先汝寧光州人。

translations.literal: Zhou Quan—his ancestors were people of Guang prefecture in Runing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Quan's ancestors came from Guang prefecture in Runing.

sentences.zh: 仕宋為武翼大夫、廣南西路馬步軍副總管。

translations.literal: He served Song as Grand Master of Martial Wings and deputy commander-in-chief of cavalry and infantry of the Guangnan West circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He had served Song as Grand Master of Martial Wings and deputy commander of the Guangnan West circuit's horse and foot forces.

sentences.zh: 至元十二年，丞相伯顏總兵下江南，全率眾來歸，遂以行省檄遙授衡州知州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhiyuan Chancellor Bayan commanded troops south of the Yangzi; Quan led his followers to surrender, and by regional secretariat dispatch was remotely appointed prefect of Heng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 12, when Bayan invaded the south, Quan surrendered with his forces and was remotely appointed prefect of Hengzhou by regional dispatch.

sentences.zh: 是年秋七月，入覲，賜金符，授明威將軍，遙授泉州知州，兼管軍千戶。

translations.literal: That autumn in the seventh month he entered court for an audience, was granted a gold tally, appointed General of Manifest Authority, remotely appointed prefect of Quan prefecture, and concurrently made army chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: That seventh month he came to court, received a gold tally, was made General of Manifest Authority and remotely appointed Quanzhou prefect, with the army chiliarch post.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，從元帥宋都下江西諸城邑。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter he followed Marshal Song Du in reducing the cities and towns of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth winter month he followed Marshal Song Du in reducing Jiangxi's cities.

sentences.zh: 明年，進兵福建，宋制置使黃萬石降。

translations.literal: The next year the army advanced into Fujian; the Song commissioner Huang Wanshi surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he advanced into Fujian; Song Commissioner Huang Wanshi surrendered.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，從大軍徵廣東，十一月，至韶州城下，嚴攻具，率勇士先登，與宋兵合戰，斬馘甚眾，殺其安撫使熊飛。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter he followed the great army to campaign in Guangdong. In the eleventh month they reached below the walls of Shao prefecture; siege equipment was prepared in earnest. He led stalwarts in the first ascent, joined battle with Song troops, beheaded very many, and killed their pacification commissioner Xiong Fei.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he joined the Guangdong campaign; in the eleventh month at Shaozhou he led the first assault, killed many in battle, and slew Pacification Commissioner Xiong Fei.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以遊騎巡廣中，過靈星海石門，敵勢甚張，全奮戈殺敵，乘勝奪其旗鼓，火其船。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month with mobile cavalry he patrolled central Guang, passing Lingxing Sea and Shimen. The enemy's force was very strong; Quan wielded his halberd fiercely to kill the enemy, seized the moment of victory to seize their banners and drums, and burned their boats.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he patrolled central Guang with light cavalry; at Lingxing Sea and Shimen the enemy was strong, but Quan fought fiercely, seized their banners and drums, and burned their ships.

sentences.zh: 及諸軍下廣州，全功居多。

translations.literal: When the various armies took Guangzhou, Quan's merit was the greater part.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies took Guangzhou, Quan's contribution was the greatest.

sentences.zh: 十四年，從攻廣西靜江府，宋安撫李夢龍率眾來降。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he followed the attack on Jingjiang prefecture in Guangxi; the Song pacification commissioner Li Menglong led his followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen he joined the assault on Jingjiang in Guangxi; Song Pacification Commissioner Li Menglong surrendered with his forces.

sentences.zh: 其有負固不下者，悉戰敗之，奪敵艦以千計，殺敵溺死者無算，兩廣以平。

translations.literal: Those who stubbornly held and would not submit were all defeated in battle; enemy ships were captured by the thousand; enemies killed and drowned were beyond count; the two Guang were thus pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Every holdout was beaten in battle; they seized enemy ships by the thousand and killed or drowned countless foes, and the two Guang provinces were pacified.

sentences.zh: 第功，賜虎符，授管軍總管。

translations.literal: For ranking merit, he was granted a tiger tally and appointed commander-in-chief of troops.
translations.idiomatic: When his merits were ranked, he received a tiger tally and was made commander-in-chief of the army.

sentences.zh: 十五年，盜據贛州崖石山寨，全率兵討平之，焚其寨。

translations.literal: In year fifteen, bandits seized the Yanshi mountain fort in Ganzhou; Quan led troops to suppress and pacify them and burned the fort.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifteen, when bandits occupied the Yanshi mountain fort at Ganzhou, Quan led troops to crush them and burned the stronghold.

sentences.zh: 十七年，進廣威將軍、管軍副萬戶，鎮守龍興。

translations.literal: In year seventeen, he was promoted to General of Expansive Might and deputy myriarch commander of troops, garrisoning Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: In year seventeen he was promoted to General of Expansive Might and deputy army myriarch, and posted to garrison Longxing.

sentences.zh: 二十年，以疾去官。

translations.literal: In year twenty, he resigned office due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty he left office because of illness.

sentences.zh: 大德九年，卒，贈懷遠大將軍、南安寨兵萬戶府萬戶、輕車都尉，追封汝南郡侯。

translations.literal: In Dad 9 he died; posthumously granted Grand General of Cherishing the Distant, myriarch of the Nan'an Fort garrison command, and Commandant of Light Chariots; posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Runan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Dad 9 and was posthumously made Grand General of Cherishing the Distant, myriarch of the Nan'an Fort command, and Commandant of Light Chariots, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Runan.

sentences.zh: 子祖瑞，襲職。

translations.literal: His son Zurui inherited the post.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zurui succeeded to the office.

sentences.zh: ○孔元

translations.literal: Kong Yuan
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yuan

sentences.zh: 孔元，字彥亨，真定人，驍勇有智略。

translations.literal: Kong Yuan, courtesy name Yanheng, was a native of Zhending; fierce and brave, with resourceful schemes.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yuan, styled Yanheng, came from Zhending. He was fierce in battle and clever in counsel.

sentences.zh: 歲丁酉，棄家從軍，隸丞相史天澤麾下。

translations.literal: In the dingyou year he abandoned his family to join the army and served under Chancellor Shi Tianze.
translations.idiomatic: In the dingyou year he left home for the army and entered the service of Chancellor Shi Tianze.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，從取焦湖，圍壽春，先登，拔其西堡。

translations.literal: In wuxu he followed in taking Jiao Lake, besieged Shouchun, was first to ascend, and captured its western fort.
translations.idiomatic: In wuxu he helped take Jiao Lake, besieged Shouchun, led the first assault, and seized its western fort.

sentences.zh: 己亥，從征安豐，力戰卻敵。

translations.literal: In jihai he followed the campaign against Anfeng, fought fiercely, and repelled the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In jihai he joined the campaign against Anfeng and, after hard fighting, drove the enemy back.

sentences.zh: 己酉，從圍泗州，拔之。

translations.literal: In jiyou he followed in besieging Sizhou and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: In jiyou he took part in the siege of Sizhou and helped capture the city.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，從攻五堂山寨，俘其眾以歸。

translations.literal: In xinhai he followed the attack on Wutangshan fort, captured its followers, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In xinhai he joined the assault on Wutangshan fort and returned with its garrison as prisoners.

sentences.zh: 戊午，從攻樊城，親王塔察兒命取樊西堡，元率死士挺槍大呼，擊殺數百人，斬首十九級以獻。

translations.literal: In wuwu he followed the attack on Fancheng; Prince Tacar ordered the capture of Fan's western fort; Yuan led dare-to-die soldiers with levelled spears and great shouts, struck down several hundred, and presented nineteen severed heads.
translations.idiomatic: In wuwu, during the assault on Fancheng, Prince Tacar ordered the western fort taken. Yuan led a band of volunteers forward with spears raised and battle cries, killed several hundred men, and presented nineteen heads.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，扈駕北征。

translations.literal: In Zhongtong 1 he escorted the emperor on the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongtong 1 he accompanied the emperor on the northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 二年，宣授管軍總把。

translations.literal: In year two he was formally appointed chief controller of troops.
translations.idiomatic: In year two he was formally made chief controller of the army.

sentences.zh: 至元十一年，從伐宋，為前鋒，所向克捷。

translations.literal: In Zhiyuan 11 he followed the expedition against Song as vanguard; wherever he went victory was achieved.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 11 he joined the campaign against Song as vanguard and won wherever he fought.

sentences.zh: 十四年，進武略將軍、管軍千戶。

translations.literal: In year fourteen he was promoted to General of Martial Strategy and army chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen he was promoted to General of Martial Strategy and army chiliarch.

sentences.zh: 明年，還軍北征，進武義將軍、侍衛親軍千戶，賜佩金符。

translations.literal: The next year, returning with the army on the northern expedition, he was promoted to General of Martial Righteousness and imperial guard chiliarch and granted a gold tally to wear.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, on the return north with the army, he was made General of Martial Righteousness and imperial guard chiliarch and given a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 又明年，國兵討叛王失里木等，從行院別乞裡迷失追其眾至兀速洋而還。

translations.literal: The year after that, when the imperial army campaigned against the rebel princes Shilimu and others, he followed the mobile headquarters chief Begülümis in pursuing their forces to Wusuyang and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when the imperial army moved against the rebel princes Shilimu and others, he followed the field headquarters chief Begülümis in pursuit to Wusuyang and then returned.

sentences.zh: 分軍之半，扼其要害地，餘眾遂潰，獲輜重牛馬。

translations.literal: He divided half the army to block their vital ground; the remainder then collapsed; they captured baggage, oxen, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: He sent half his force to hold the enemy's line of retreat; the rest broke and fled, and they seized wagons, oxen, and horses.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賞賚甚厚，加宣武將軍、右衛親軍總管。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, rewarded him richly, and added the titles General of Manifest Martiality and commander of the Right Guard imperial troops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and rewarded him generously, making him General of Manifest Martiality and commander of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 十九年，以疾卒。

translations.literal: In year nineteen he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in year nineteen.

sentences.zh: ○硃國寶

translations.literal: Zhu Guobao
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Guobao

sentences.zh: 硃國寶，其先徐州人，後徙寶坻。

translations.literal: Zhu Guobao—his ancestors were people of Xuzhou; later they moved to Baodi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Guobao's family originally came from Xuzhou and later moved to Baodi.

sentences.zh: 父存器，歷官至修內司使。

translations.literal: His father Cunqi rose through offices to Commissioner of the Bureau of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cunqi rose through the ranks to become Commissioner of the Bureau of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜行盧溝橋，獲金一囊，坐而待其主以付之，其人請中分，存器笑而遣之。

translations.literal: Once traveling at night on the Lugou Bridge, he found a bag of gold; he sat and waited for its owner to return it; the man asked to split it; Cunqi smiled and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Once, walking at night on the Lugou Bridge, he found a bag of gold, sat down, and waited for the owner. When the man arrived and asked to split it, Cunqi smiled and refused.

sentences.zh: 憲宗將攻宋，募兵習水戰，國寶以職官子從軍，隸水軍萬戶解誠麾下。

translations.literal: When Emperor Möngke was about to attack Song, he recruited soldiers trained in naval warfare; Guobao, as the son of an official, joined the army and served under naval myriarch Jie Cheng.
