translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Möngke prepared to attack Song, he recruited men trained in river warfare. Guobao, the son of an official, enlisted and served under the naval myriarch Jie Cheng.

sentences.zh: 己未，世祖以兵攻鄂，國寶攝千戶，率銳卒於中流與宋師鏖戰，凡十七戰，諸軍畢濟。

translations.literal: In jiwei Kublai attacked E with troops; Guobao acted as chiliarch, led elite soldiers in midstream to fight fiercely with Song forces—in all seventeen battles—and all armies crossed completely.
translations.idiomatic: In jiwei, when Kublai attacked Ezhou, Guobao served as acting chiliarch and led crack troops in seventeen midstream battles with the Song fleet until the whole army had crossed.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，授千戶，佩銀符。

translations.literal: In Zhongtong 2 he was appointed chiliarch and wore a silver tally.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongtong 2 he was made chiliarch and given a silver tally.

sentences.zh: 三年，圍李璮於濟南，佩金符，鎮戍東海。

translations.literal: In year three, when Li Tan was besieged at Jinan, he wore a gold tally and garrisoned the Eastern Sea.
translations.idiomatic: In year three, while Li Tan was besieged at Jinan, he wore a gold tally and garrisoned the Eastern Sea.

sentences.zh: 從征襄陽，攝四翼鎮撫，督造戰艦，築萬山堡。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Xiangyang, acted as pacifier of the four wings, supervised construction of warships, and built Wanshan fort.
translations.idiomatic: On the Xiangyang campaign he served as acting pacifier of the four wings, oversaw the building of warships, and constructed Wanshan fort.

sentences.zh: 至元十一年，拔沙洋，隳新城，皆與有力焉。

translations.literal: In Zhiyuan 11, in capturing Shayang and destroying Xincheng, he contributed significant force in both.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 11 he played a major part in taking Shayang and destroying Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 初，師次江上，國寶請於丞相伯顏，願當前鋒，既而奪船二十艘以獻，伯顏壯之。

translations.literal: Initially when the army halted on the river, Guobao requested of Chancellor Bayan that he wished to take the vanguard; thereafter he seized twenty boats and presented them; Bayan admired this.
translations.idiomatic: When the army first halted on the Yangzi, Guobao asked Chancellor Bayan to let him lead the vanguard, then captured twenty boats and presented them. Bayan was impressed.

sentences.zh: 宋據上流，方舟數百，結為堡柵，伯顏指示曰：「復能奪取是乎？」

translations.literal: Song held the upper river; several hundred boats were linked as fort palisades; Bayan pointed and said: "Can you again seize these?"
translations.idiomatic: The Song held the upper river with several hundred boats chained into a fortified barrier. Bayan pointed and asked, "Can you take those as well?"

sentences.zh: 國寶即奮往破柵。

translations.literal: Guobao at once charged forward and broke the palisades.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao charged at once and broke the barrier.

sentences.zh: 既渡江，下鄂、漢。

translations.literal: Having crossed the river, they took E and Han.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the river, they took Ezhou and Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 十二年，進兵臨岳州，與宋兵戰於岳之桃花灘，獲其將高世傑，進昭信校尉、管軍總管。

translations.literal: In year twelve, advancing to threaten Yuezhou, he fought Song troops at Taohua Shoals in Yue, captured their general Gao Shijie, and was promoted to Commandant of Manifest Trust and commander-in-chief of troops.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve he advanced on Yuezhou, defeated the Song at Taohua Shoals, captured General Gao Shijie, and was promoted to Commandant of Manifest Trust and army commander.

sentences.zh: 既降湖右，加宣武將軍，統蒙古諸軍，鎮常德府，知安撫司事。

translations.literal: After the right of the lake surrendered, he was given General of Manifest Martiality, commanded the various Mongol armies, garrisoned Changde prefecture, and directed pacification office affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the region west of the lakes submitted, he was made General of Manifest Martiality, placed in command of the Mongol forces, and posted to Changde as head of the pacification office.

sentences.zh: 時宋諸郡邑多堅守不下，國寶傳檄招諭，踰月悉平，惟辰、沅、靖、鎮遠未下。

translations.literal: At the time many Song prefectures and counties stubbornly held and would not submit; Guobao sent proclamations to summon and instruct; within a month all were pacified; only Chen, Yuan, Jing, and Zhenyuan had not fallen.
translations.idiomatic: Many Song prefectures and counties still held out, but within a month Guobao's proclamations had pacified nearly all of them; only Chen, Yuan, Jing, and Zhenyuan remained.

sentences.zh: 宋將李信、李發結武岡洞蠻，分據扼寨，國寶擊敗之，其眾退保飛山、新城。

translations.literal: Song generals Li Xin and Li Fa joined with Wugang cave barbarians, divided forces to hold strategic forts; Guobao defeated them; their forces withdrew to defend Feishan and Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Song generals Li Xin and Li Fa allied with the Wugang cave peoples and held strategic forts, but Guobao defeated them and drove them back to Feishan and Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 思、播蠻來援，國寶復與戰，破之，擒張星、沈舉等三百餘人。

translations.literal: Si and Bo barbarians came to reinforce; Guobao again fought and broke them, capturing Zhang Xing, Shen Ju, and more than three hundred others.
translations.idiomatic: When Si and Bo reinforcements arrived, Guobao fought them again, broke their force, and captured Zhang Xing, Shen Ju, and more than three hundred men.

sentences.zh: 進攻新城，獲信、發等，獻俘江陵。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Xincheng, he captured Xin, Fa, and others and presented prisoners at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He then attacked Xincheng, captured Li Xin, Li Fa, and their followers, and presented the prisoners at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 行省奏功，賜金虎符。

translations.literal: The regional secretariat memorialized his merit; he was granted a gold tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: The regional secretariat reported his achievements, and he received a gold tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 十四年，會諸道兵攻廣西靜江，拔之，進秩管軍萬戶，鎮守梧州，領安撫司事。

translations.literal: In year fourteen, joining troops from various circuits to attack Jingjiang in Guangxi, they captured it; his rank was advanced to army myriarch; he garrisoned Wuzhou and headed pacification office affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen he joined forces from several circuits in taking Jingjiang in Guangxi, was promoted to army myriarch, and was posted to Wuzhou as head of the pacification office.

sentences.zh: 十五年，加懷遠大將軍。

translations.literal: In year fifteen he was given the additional title Grand General of Cherishing the Distant.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifteen he was additionally made Grand General of Cherishing the Distant.

sentences.zh: 初，宋臨安之破也，張世傑挾二王由閩蹈海，眾复滋蔓。

translations.literal: Initially when Song's Lin'an fell, Zhang Shijie took the two princes from Fujian to sea; forces again spread luxuriantly.
translations.idiomatic: After Lin'an fell, Zhang Shijie fled to sea from Fujian with the two Song princes, and resistance flared up again.

sentences.zh: 時南恩、新州何華、張翼，舉兵興復，軍勢甚盛。

translations.literal: At the time He Hua and Zhang Yi of Nan'en and Xin prefectures raised troops for restoration; their military strength was very great.
translations.idiomatic: At Nan'en and Xinzhou, He Hua and Zhang Yi raised armies to restore Song rule, and their forces grew very strong.

sentences.zh: 國寶選精銳，擊殺華、翼，擒其黨二人，斬首萬餘級，俘五百餘人、船七百艘，奪其兵器無算，降其將十餘、軍士二百、民三萬餘戶。

translations.literal: Guobao selected crack troops, struck down Hua and Yi, captured two of their partisans, beheaded more than ten thousand, took more than five hundred prisoners and seven hundred boats, seized weapons beyond count, and received the surrender of more than ten generals, two hundred soldiers, and more than thirty thousand households of common people.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao chose elite troops, killed He Hua and Zhang Yi, captured two of their lieutenants, took more than ten thousand heads, five hundred prisoners, and seven hundred boats, seized countless weapons, and received the surrender of more than ten officers, two hundred soldiers, and over thirty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 十六年，遷定遠大將軍、海北海南道宣慰使。

translations.literal: In year sixteen he was transferred to Grand General of Settling the Distant and pacification commissioner of the Haibei and Hainan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In year sixteen he was transferred to Grand General of Settling the Distant and pacification commissioner of the Haibei-Hainan circuit.

sentences.zh: 蜑賊連結鬱林、廉州諸洞，恣行剽掠，國寶悉平之，磔屍高化，以懲反側。

translations.literal: Dan bandits linked with the caves of Yulin and Lian prefectures, wantonly raiding and plundering; Guobao pacified them all, dismembered corpses at Gaohua as a warning to the restive.
translations.idiomatic: Dan bandits joined with the cave peoples of Yulin and Lianzhou in widespread raids. Guobao suppressed them all and displayed dismembered corpses at Gaohua to warn the rebellious.

sentences.zh: 任龍光等率所部五千戶降。

translations.literal: Ren Longguang and others led their divisions of five thousand households to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Longguang and others surrendered with their five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 移瓊州，立官程，更弊政，訓兵息民，具有條製。

translations.literal: Transferred to Qiongzhou, he established official procedures, reformed corrupt policies, trained soldiers and rested the people, with comprehensive regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Posted to Qiongzhou, he set official procedures, reformed bad government, trained troops and eased the burden on the people, and put clear regulations in place.

sentences.zh: 南寧謝有奎負固不服，國寶開示信義，有奎感悟，以其屬來歸。

translations.literal: Xie Youkui of Nan'ning stubbornly refused submission; Guobao opened with trust and righteousness; Youkui was moved and came with his followers to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Youkui of Nan'ning stubbornly refused to submit, but Guobao won him over with trust and righteousness, and Youkui came in with his followers.

sentences.zh: 於是黎民降者三千戶，蠻洞降者三十所。

translations.literal: Thereupon three thousand households of common people surrendered, and thirty barbarian cave settlements submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand common households and thirty cave settlements then submitted.

sentences.zh: 十八年，破臨高蠻寇五百人，招降居亥、番亳、銅鼓、博吐、桐油等十九洞，遣部將韓旺率兵略大黎、密塘、橫山，誅首惡李實，火其巢，生致大鐘、小鍾諸部長十有八人，加鎮國上將軍、海北海南道宣慰使都元帥。

translations.literal: In year eighteen he defeated five hundred Lin'gao barbarian raiders, summoned and received the submission of nineteen caves including Juha, Fanmo, Tonggu, Botu, and Tongyou; sent subordinate general Han Wang to lead troops in reducing Dali, Mitang, and Hengshan, executed the chief villain Li Shi, burned their nest, and brought alive eighteen chieftains including Dazhong and Xiaozhong; added Grand General of Pacifying the State and commander-in-chief pacification commissioner of the Haibei-Hainan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In year eighteen he defeated five hundred Lin'gao raiders, brought nineteen caves including Juha, Fanmo, Tonggu, Botu, and Tongyou to surrender, and sent Han Wang against Dali, Mitang, and Hengshan. Li Shi, the ringleader, was executed and his stronghold burned; eighteen chieftains including Dazhong and Xiaozhong were taken alive. He was then made Grand General of Pacifying the State and commander-in-chief of the Haibei-Hainan pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 供給占城軍餉，事集而民不擾。

translations.literal: He supplied rations for the Champa campaign; affairs were completed without disturbing the people.
translations.idiomatic: He supplied provisions for the Champa campaign and accomplished the task without troubling the people.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，遷廣南西道宣慰使。

translations.literal: In year twenty-three he was transferred to pacification commissioner of the Guangnan West circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-three he was transferred to pacification commissioner of the Guangnan West circuit.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，入覲，帝慰勞之。

translations.literal: In year twenty-four he entered court for audience; the emperor comforted and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-four he came to court, and the emperor received and praised him.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，進輔國上將軍、都元帥、參知政事，行尚書省事。

translations.literal: In year twenty-five he was promoted to Grand General of Assisting the State, commander-in-chief, vice administrator of affairs, exercising Ministry of Works affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-five he was promoted to Grand General of Assisting the State, commander-in-chief, and vice administrator of affairs with charge of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 以軍事至贛州，得疾，卒於傳舍，年五十九。

translations.literal: On military business he reached Ganzhou, fell ill, and died at a relay station, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: While on campaign he reached Ganzhou, fell ill, and died at a relay station at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 子斌，襲職，累官加賜金虎符、海北海南宣慰使都元帥。

translations.literal: His son Bin inherited the post, accumulating offices and additionally granted a gold tiger tally and commander pacification commissioner of Haibei-Hainan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bin succeeded to the office, rose through further appointments, and was additionally granted a gold tiger tally as commander of the Haibei-Hainan pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 贇，上副萬戶，佩金虎符，鎮福州。

translations.literal: Yun, senior deputy myriarch, wore a gold tiger tally and garrisoned Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yun served as senior deputy myriarch with a gold tiger tally and garrisoned Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 次鼎；

translations.literal: Next, Ding;
translations.idiomatic: Next was Ding;

sentences.zh: 次鉉。

translations.literal: Next, Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: then Xuan.

sentences.zh: ○張立

translations.literal: Zhang Li
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Li

sentences.zh: 張立，泰安長清人。

translations.literal: Zhang Li was a native of Changqing in Tai'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Li came from Changqing in Tai'an.

sentences.zh: 初隸嚴實麾下，略江淮有功，署為百戶。

translations.literal: Initially he served under Yan Shi; in reducing Jianghuai he had merit and was appointed centurion.
translations.idiomatic: He first served under Yan Shi and, for his achievements in campaigns along the Yangzi and Huai, was appointed centurion.

sentences.zh: 歲戊午，憲宗徵蜀，徵諸道兵，立從行。

translations.literal: In the wuwu year Emperor Möngke campaigned against Shu and summoned troops from all circuits; Li followed.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuwu year, when Emperor Möngke campaigned against Shu and called up troops from every circuit, Li went with the army.

sentences.zh: 次大獲山，宋人阻山為城，帶江為池，恃以自固，立統銳卒，攻陷外堡，奪戰船百餘艘。

translations.literal: At Dahu Mountain, Song men blocked the mountain as a city wall and used the river as a moat, relying on these to hold firm; Li commanded crack soldiers, stormed the outer fort, and seized more than a hundred warships.
translations.idiomatic: At Dahu Mountain the Song had fortified the heights and used the river as a moat. Li led crack troops, stormed the outer fort, and captured more than a hundred warships.

sentences.zh: 復從攻釣魚山，有功，賜金帛。

translations.literal: Again he followed the attack on Diaoyu Mountain, had merit, and was granted gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: He also took part in the assault on Diaoyu Mountain, distinguished himself, and was rewarded with gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 中統初，從世祖北征，還，授管軍總把，賜銀符，進侍衛軍鎮撫，換金符，改侍衛軍千戶。

translations.literal: In early Zhongtong he followed Kublai on the northern expedition; upon return he was appointed chief controller of troops, granted a silver tally, advanced to imperial guard pacifier, exchanged for a gold tally, and changed to imperial guard chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: In early Zhongtong he followed Kublai on the northern campaign. On his return he was made chief controller of troops with a silver tally, then imperial guard pacifier with a gold tally, and finally imperial guard chiliarch.

sentences.zh: 尋遷左衛親軍副都指揮使，賜金虎符。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to deputy commander of the Left Guard imperial troops and granted a gold tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made deputy commander of the Left Guard and given a gold tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 十四年春，率步卒千人轉粟赴和林​​，道出應昌。

translations.literal: In the spring of year fourteen he led a thousand foot soldiers to transport grain to Karakorum; the route passed through Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year fourteen he led a thousand foot soldiers to haul grain to Karakorum by way of Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 會酋帥畔換謀不軌，以射士三千踵其後，欲乘間奪其資糧。

translations.literal: He encountered the tribal chief Panhuan plotting treason, who with three thousand archers followed behind, intending to seize his provisions at an opportune moment.
translations.idiomatic: There he met the tribal chief Panhuan plotting rebellion. Panhuan followed with three thousand archers, hoping to seize Li's supplies at a weak moment.

sentences.zh: 立覺其有異，急命環車為柵以備之。

translations.literal: Li sensed something amiss and urgently ordered wagons circled as palisades for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Li sensed trouble and immediately ordered the wagons formed into a circular barricade.

sentences.zh: 賊眾已合，矢如雨下。

translations.literal: The bandit force had already gathered; arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy closed in and arrows fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 初，立之發上都也，每車載二板，以備不虞。

translations.literal: Initially when Li departed Shangdu, each wagon carried two boards against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: When Li had left Shangdu, he had had each wagon carry two boards against the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 至是，建板於車，矢不能入，騎卒稍前，即以戈撞之，強弩繼發，賊不得近。

translations.literal: At this point boards were set on the wagons; arrows could not enter; when mounted soldiers advanced slightly, they were struck with halberds; powerful crossbows followed; bandits could not approach.
translations.idiomatic: Now the boards were raised on the wagons so arrows could not penetrate. When enemy horsemen came close, his men struck them with halberds and followed with heavy crossbows, and the attackers could not break in.

sentences.zh: 相持連日，乃解去。

translations.literal: They faced off for consecutive days, then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The standoff lasted several days before the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是歲，增置前後衛兵，進明威將軍、後衛親軍都指揮使，賜雙珠虎符，加昭勇大將軍，以老乞退。

translations.literal: That year front and rear guard troops were added; he was promoted to General of Manifest Authority and commander of the Rear Guard imperial troops, granted a double-pearl tiger tally, given Grand General of Manifest Valor, and requested retirement due to age.
translations.idiomatic: That year, when front and rear guard units were expanded, he was made General of Manifest Authority and commander of the Rear Guard, given a double-pearl tiger tally and the additional rank of Grand General of Manifest Valor, then retired on account of age.

sentences.zh: 子圭襲。

translations.literal: His son Gui inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gui succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 圭卒，子伯潛襲。

translations.literal: When Gui died, his son Boqian inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui died, his son Boqian succeeded to the office.

sentences.zh: ○齊秉節

translations.literal: Qi Bingjie
translations.idiomatic: Qi Bingjie

sentences.zh: 齊秉節，字子度，濱州蒲台人。

translations.literal: Qi Bingjie, courtesy name Zidu, was a native of Putai in Bin prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Bingjie, styled Zidu, came from Putai in Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 父圭，從嚴實攻歸德、廬州，有功，授無棣縣尹，攝徵行千戶，後兼總管，鎮棗陽。

translations.literal: His father Gui followed Yan Shi in attacking Guide and Luzhou, had merit, was appointed magistrate of Wudi county, acted as mobile requisition chiliarch, later concurrently commander, garrisoning Zaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gui followed Yan Shi in the capture of Guide and Luzhou, was rewarded with appointment as magistrate of Wudi, served as acting mobile requisition chiliarch, later became commander as well, and garrisoned Zaoyang.

sentences.zh: 中統三年，李璮以益都叛，徵諸道兵進討，棗陽精銳盡行，僅留羸卒千餘。

translations.literal: In Zhongtong 3 Li Tan rebelled from Yidu; troops from all circuits were summoned to campaign; Zaoyang's crack forces all marched out; only slightly more than a thousand weak soldiers remained.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongtong 3, when Li Tan rebelled from Yidu and troops were called up from every circuit, Zaoyang sent out all its best soldiers and left barely a thousand weak men behind.

sentences.zh: 圭時攝萬戶府事，與宋襄、郢對壘。

translations.literal: At the time Gui acted as myriarch office affairs, facing Song across the lines at Xiang and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was then acting head of the myriarch office, facing Song forces across the lines from Xiangyang and Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 敵來覘虛實，圭城守周密，以東門外壕狹小可越，命濬之為備。

translations.literal: The enemy came to scout strength and weakness; Gui's city defense was thorough; seeing the moat outside the east gate was narrow enough to cross, he ordered it deepened as preparation.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy came to probe the defenses, Gui found the moat outside the east gate too narrow to stop an assault and ordered it deepened.

sentences.zh: 宋將聶都統、陳總管果率兵萬餘抵城東門，以板渡壕，壕廣，板不能及，圭率眾力戰，敵退走，城賴以完。

translations.literal: Song generals Commander Nie and Supervisor Chen indeed led more than ten thousand troops to the east gate, using boards to cross the moat; the moat was wide and boards could not reach; Gui led the masses in fierce battle; the enemy withdrew; the city was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: Song commanders Nie and Chen did indeed bring more than ten thousand men to the east gate and tried to bridge the moat with planks, but the widened ditch was too broad. Gui led a hard fight and drove them off, saving the city.

sentences.zh: 事聞，賜金符，真授千戶。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was granted a gold tally and formally appointed chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached court, he received a gold tally and a formal appointment as chiliarch.

sentences.zh: 至元三年，告老，舉秉節自代。

translations.literal: In Zhiyuan 3 he reported old age and recommended Bingjie to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 3 he retired on account of age and recommended Bingjie as his successor.

sentences.zh: 秉節魁偉沈毅，涉獵書史，稍知兵法，襲父爵，仍鎮棗陽。

translations.literal: Bingjie was imposing and steady, dipped into books and histories, knew somewhat of military arts, inherited his father's rank, and still garrisoned Zaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Bingjie was tall and steady, well read in history, and versed in military affairs. He inherited his father's rank and continued to garrison Zaoyang.

sentences.zh: 五年，從伐宋，築新城白河口堡鹿門山，略地郢州大洪山黃仙洞，數著戰功。

translations.literal: In year five he followed the campaign against Song, built the new fort at Baihekou and Lumen Mountain, reduced territory at Dahong Mountain and Huangxian Cave in Ying prefecture, and repeatedly achieved battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he joined the campaign against Song, built forts at Baihekou and Lumen Mountain, and took ground around Dahong Mountain and Huangxian Cave in Yingzhou, winning repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 七年，升上千戶，權萬戶。

translations.literal: In year seven he was promoted to senior chiliarch, acting myriarch.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven he was promoted to senior chiliarch with acting myriarch authority.

sentences.zh: 十一年，從丞相伯顏至郢，蕩舟由陸入江，攻武磯堡，擒宋將閻都統。

translations.literal: In year eleven he followed Chancellor Bayan to Ying, floated boats from land into the river, attacked Wuji fort, and captured Song general Commander Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven he followed Chancellor Bayan to Yingzhou, launched boats from land into the river, assaulted Wuji fort, and captured Song Commander Yan.

sentences.zh: 十二年，國兵敗宋賈似道、孫虎臣舟師於丁家洲，命秉節屯建康，與宋將趙淮戰於西離山，追至溧陽，自辰及午，宋軍乃退。

translations.literal: In year twelve the imperial army defeated Song naval forces of Jia Sidao and Sun Huchen at Dingjiazhou; Bingjie was ordered to encamp at Jiankang; he fought Song general Zhao Huai at Xili Mountain, pursued to Liyang; from the chen hour to the wu hour the Song army then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve, after the imperial fleet defeated Jia Sidao and Sun Huchen at Dingjiazhou, Bingjie was posted at Jiankang. He fought Zhao Huai at Xili Mountain, pursued him to Liyang, and battled from morning until noon before the Song army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 八月，遷武義將軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was transferred to General of Martial Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was made General of Martial Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 十二月，從定太平、安慶諸郡，與宋將張諮議戰於崑山，殺之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he followed in pacifying Taiping, Anqing, and other commanderies; fought Song adviser-general Zhang at Kunshan and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he helped pacify Taiping, Anqing, and other commanderies, fought Song Adviser-General Zhang at Kunshan, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 十四年，授宣武將軍、管軍總管。

translations.literal: In year fourteen he was appointed General of Manifest Martiality and army commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was appointed General of Manifest Martiality and commander-in-chief of the army.

sentences.zh: 時黃州复叛，令秉節往討，斬餘總轄於陣。

translations.literal: At that time Huang prefecture again rebelled; Bingjie was ordered to go suppress it and beheaded Yu Zongguan in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhou rebelled again, and Bingjie was sent to suppress the revolt. He beheaded Commander Yu in the field.

sentences.zh: 十七年，授明威將軍。

translations.literal: In year seventeen he was appointed General of Bright Prestige.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was made General of Bright Prestige.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，移鎮饒州。

translations.literal: In year twenty-three he was transferred to garrison Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was transferred to garrison Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 安仁劇賊蔡福一叛，秉節與有司會兵討之，擒福一，餘黨悉平。

translations.literal: The fierce bandit Cai Fuyi of Anren rebelled; Bingjie joined officials in converging troops to suppress him, captured Fuyi, and all remaining partisans were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Fuyi, a notorious bandit of Anren, rose in rebellion. Bingjie joined forces with local officials to suppress him, captured Fuyi, and pacified all remaining rebels.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，升廣威將軍、棗陽萬戶府副萬戶。

translations.literal: In year twenty-five he was promoted to General of Broad Prestige and deputy myriarch of the Zaoyang Myriarchy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted to General of Broad Prestige and made deputy myriarch of the Zaoyang Myriarchy.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，卒，年六十二。

translations.literal: In year twenty-eight he died, age sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he died at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 子英襲。

translations.literal: His son Ying succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ying inherited the post.

sentences.zh: ○張萬家奴

translations.literal: Zhangwan Jianu
translations.idiomatic: Zhangwan Jianu

sentences.zh: 張萬家奴，父札古帶，事睿宗於潛邸。

translations.literal: Zhangwan Jianu—his father Zhagudai served Prince Ruizong at the hidden residence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangwan Jianu was the son of Zhagudai, who had served Prince Ruizong at his princely residence.

sentences.zh: 從破金有功，賜虎符，授河東南北路船橋隨路兵馬都總管萬戶。

translations.literal: Following in breaking Jin he had merit; was granted a tiger tally and appointed myriarch as overall commander of ships, bridges, and route troops of the North and South Circuits of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He fought in the conquest of Jin with distinction, received a tiger tally, and was appointed myriarch and overall commander of ships, bridges, and route forces across the North and South Circuits of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 從西征，下興元，圍嘉定，歿於軍。

translations.literal: Following the western expedition he took Xingyuan, besieged Jiading, and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: On the western expedition he took Xingyuan and besieged Jiading, but died in camp.

sentences.zh: 萬家奴數從都元帥大答火魯征討，有功。

translations.literal: Jianu repeatedly followed Grand General Dadahuo'er on campaigns and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Jianu repeatedly campaigned under Grand General Dadahuo'er and won distinction.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，從都元帥紐璘入朝，授以父官。

translations.literal: In Zhongtong 2 he followed Grand General Niulin to court and was granted his father's office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongtong he accompanied Grand General Niulin to court and received his father's post.

sentences.zh: 宋兵入成都，從行院阿脫擊破之。

translations.literal: Song troops entered Chengdu; he followed the Mobile Bureau's Atu in defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: When Song forces entered Chengdu, he followed Mobile Bureau commander Atu and routed them.

sentences.zh: 至元四年，帥師會立眉、簡二州。

translations.literal: In Zhiyuan 4 he led troops to join in establishing Mei and Jian prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 4 he led troops to help establish Mei and Jian prefectures.

sentences.zh: 從也速答兒攻瀘州，大敗宋軍，殺傷過半，俘四十餘人以歸。

translations.literal: Following Yasudar he attacked Luzhou, heavily defeated Song forces—more than half killed and wounded—and returned with over forty captives.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Yasudar's assault on Luzhou, crushing the Song army with casualties exceeding half their strength, and returned with more than forty prisoners.

sentences.zh: 七年，率諸軍城張廣平，與宋人戰，斬首三百餘級，獲都統一人。

translations.literal: In year seven he led various armies to fortify Zhangguangping; fighting Song men he beheaded over three hundred heads and captured one commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he led his forces to build fortifications at Zhangguangping. In battle with the Song he took over three hundred heads and captured a commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 從攻重慶，破朝陽寨，圍嘉定，柵平康、太和、懷遠諸寨，分兵以守之，且日出師，水陸接戰，功居多。

translations.literal: Following the attack on Chongqing he broke Chaoyang stockade, besieged Jiading, palisaded Pingkang, Taihe, Huaiyuan and other stockades, divided troops to hold them, and every day sallied forth; water and land engaged in succession—his merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Chongqing he stormed Chaoyang stockade and besieged Jiading. He fortified Pingkang, Taihe, Huaiyuan, and other stockades, garrisoning them with detachments. Day after day he led combined land-and-water attacks, and his contribution stood foremost among the commanders.

sentences.zh: 而諸將攻瀘州，往往失利，乃詣闕請自任以攻取之效，許之。

translations.literal: But when various generals attacked Luzhou they often met defeat; he therefore went to the capital to request personally undertaking to show the effect of taking it—and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Other generals had repeatedly failed to take Luzhou, so he went to court and volunteered to capture the city himself. His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 遂率舟師百五十艘，自桃竹灘至折魚灘，分守江面，謹風火，嚴號令，約日進攻。

translations.literal: He then led a fleet of one hundred fifty vessels from Taozhu Beach to Zheyu Beach, dividing guard over the river surface, carefully managing signal fires, strictly enforcing orders, and setting a day for the assault.
translations.idiomatic: He then commanded a fleet of one hundred fifty vessels from Taozhu Beach to Zheyu Beach, blockading the river. Signal fires were kept ready, orders were rigorously enforced, and a date was fixed for the assault.

sentences.zh: 先據神臂門，為梯衝登城，殺二百餘人，斬關而入，遂拔之，加昭勇大將軍。

translations.literal: First seizing the Divine Arm Gate, with scaling ladders and rams he mounted the wall, killed over two hundred men, cut through the gate and entered, then took it; he was promoted to Grand General of Manifest Valor.
translations.idiomatic: He seized the Divine Arm Gate first, scaled the walls with siege ladders and rams, killed more than two hundred defenders, broke through the gate, and captured the city. He was promoted to Grand General of Manifest Valor.

sentences.zh: 會圍重慶，將其眾斷馬湖江，分兵水陸往來為遊徼，加昭毅大將軍。

translations.literal: When besieging Chongqing he led his troops to block the Mahu River, divided forces on water and land going back and forth as patrols, and was promoted to Grand General of Manifest Steadfastness.
translations.idiomatic: During the siege of Chongqing he blocked the Mahu River with his forces, deploying land and naval detachments in continual patrol, and was promoted to Grand General of Manifest Steadfastness.

sentences.zh: 以所部轉餉成都及下流諸屯，尋遷招討使。

translations.literal: With his command he transported provisions to Chengdu and downstream garrisons; soon he was transferred to pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He used his troops to transport supplies to Chengdu and downstream garrisons, and was soon made pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 與都元帥藥剌海討亦奚不薛蠻，平之，進副都元帥。

translations.literal: With Grand General Yarlighai he suppressed the Yixibuxi barbarians, pacified them, and was advanced to vice grand general.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Grand General Yarlighai he suppressed the Yixibuxi tribes and pacified them. He was promoted to vice grand general.

sentences.zh: 詔其子孝忠為船橋萬戶。

translations.literal: An edict made his son Xiaozhong myriarch of ships and bridges.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed his son Xiaozhong myriarch of ships and bridges.

sentences.zh: 以萬家奴將四川、湖南兵徵哈剌章。

translations.literal: Jianu was ordered to lead Sichuan and Hunan troops to campaign against Karajang.
translations.idiomatic: Jianu was ordered to lead Sichuan and Hunan troops against Karajang.

sentences.zh: 時雲南惡昌、多興、羅羅諸蠻皆叛，殺掠使者，劫奪人民，州郡莫能製，遂以其兵討之，剿其眾，民為之立祠。

translations.literal: At that time in Yunnan the Echang, Duoxing, Luoluo and other barbarians all rebelled, killed and plundered envoys, seized the people—prefectures and districts could not restrain them; he therefore used his troops to suppress them, wiped out their bands, and the people erected shrines for him.
translations.idiomatic: In Yunnan the Echang, Duoxing, Luoluo, and other tribes had all risen in revolt, murdering envoys and preying on the people. No prefecture could contain them. Jianu marched against them, destroyed their forces, and the people built shrines in his honor.

sentences.zh: 二十年，從征緬，戰死之。

translations.literal: In year twenty he followed the campaign against Burma and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he joined the Burma campaign and was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 雲南王命其子保童將其軍從征，入太公城，有功，襲副都元帥。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yunnan ordered his son Baotong to lead his army on the campaign; entering Taigong city he had merit and inherited the vice grand general rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yunnan ordered his son Baotong to take command of his father's army. Baotong fought at Taigong city with distinction and inherited the rank of vice grand general.

sentences.zh: 又從徵至甘州山丹，亦戰死。

translations.literal: Again following a campaign he reached Shandan in Gan prefecture and also died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined another campaign as far as Shandan in Ganzhou, where he too was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 孝忠少從父軍中，好攻戰。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong from youth followed his father in the army and loved attack and battle.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong had campaigned with his father from boyhood and was eager for combat.

sentences.zh: 至元十九年，從都元帥也速答兒討亦奚不薛蠻，遇其眾於會靈關，追至沙溪，敗之。

translations.literal: In Zhiyuan 19 he followed Grand General Yasudar to suppress the Yixibuxi barbarians; encountering their host at Huiling Pass he pursued to Shaxi and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 19 he joined Grand General Yasudar's campaign against the Yixibuxi tribes. He met the enemy at Huiling Pass, pursued them to Shaxi, and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 進攻龍家寨阿那關，克之，遂攻亦奚不薛營，大破之。

translations.literal: Advancing he attacked Longjia stockade and Ana Pass, took them, then attacked the Yixibuxi camp and heavily defeated it.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed Longjia stockade and Ana Pass, captured both, then assaulted the Yixibuxi encampment and routed it completely.

sentences.zh: 又以八百人敗阿永蠻於鹿札河，乘勝至打鼓寨，連破之。

translations.literal: Again with eight hundred men he defeated the Ayong barbarians at Luzha River, pressed the victory to Daguzhai, and repeatedly broke them.
translations.idiomatic: With only eight hundred men he defeated the Ayong tribes at the Luzha River, pressed the advantage to Daguzhai, and won a series of victories.

sentences.zh: 諸蠻平，以功賜金帛、弓矢、鞍轡，還軍成都。

translations.literal: When the barbarians were pacified, for merit he was granted gold and silk, bows and arrows, saddles and bridles, and returned the army to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: After the tribes were pacified, he was rewarded with gold and silk, bows and arrows, and saddlery, and returned with his troops to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，從討烏蒙蠻。

translations.literal: In year twenty-two he followed in suppressing the Wumeng barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he joined the campaign against the Wumeng tribes.

sentences.zh: 复擊降大壩都掌、蟻子諸蠻，加明威將軍。

translations.literal: Again he attacked and reduced the Daba, Duzhang, Yizi and other barbarians, and was promoted to General of Bright Prestige.
translations.idiomatic: He again attacked and subdued the Daba, Duzhang, Yizi, and other tribes, and was promoted to General of Bright Prestige.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，詔從西征，至沙、瓜諸州，還，賜虎符，僉書四川等處行樞密院事。

translations.literal: In year twenty-seven by edict he followed the western expedition to Sha, Gua and other prefectures; on return he was granted a tiger tally and appointed concurrent secretary of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat for Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he was ordered on the western expedition as far as Shazhou and Guazhou. On his return he received a tiger tally and was made concurrent secretary of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat for Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 院罷，以本軍萬戶鎮成都，卒。

translations.literal: When the bureau was abolished he garrisoned Chengdu as myriarch with his original army and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the bureau was dissolved, he garrisoned Chengdu as myriarch of his original command and died in office.

sentences.zh: ○郭昂

translations.literal: Guo Ang
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ang

sentences.zh: 郭昂，字彥高，彰德林州人。

translations.literal: Guo Ang, style Yangao, was a native of Linzhou in Zhangde.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ang, courtesy name Yangao, was a native of Linzhou in Zhangde circuit.

sentences.zh: 習刀槊，能挽強，稍通經史，尤工於詩。

translations.literal: He trained in saber and spear, could draw the strong bow, knew somewhat of classics and history, and was especially skilled at poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He was trained in the saber and spear, drew a strong bow, had some grounding in the classics and history, and was especially accomplished as a poet.

sentences.zh: 至元二年，上書言事，平章廉希憲材之，授山東統軍司知事，尋改經歷，遷襄陽總軍司，轉沅州安撫司同知，佩金符，招降溪洞八十餘柵。

translations.literal: In Zhiyuan 2 he submitted a memorial on state affairs; Vice Grand Councillor Lian Xixian recognized his talent and appointed him registrar of the Shandong Army Command; soon changed to intendant, transferred to Xiangyang General Army Command, then deputy pacification commissioner of Yuan prefecture, wearing a gold tally, and induced over eighty creek stockades to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 2 he submitted a memorial to the throne. Vice Grand Councillor Lian Xixian recognized his ability and appointed him registrar of the Shandong Army Command, then intendant, then transferred him to the Xiangyang General Army Command and made him deputy pacification commissioner of Yuanzhou with a gold tally. He induced more than eighty creek stockades to surrender.

sentences.zh: 播州張華聚眾容山，昂率兵屠之，山徭、木貓、土獠諸洞盡降。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua of Bozhou gathered a host at Rong Mountain; Ang led troops and slaughtered them; the Shan Yao, Mumao, Tuliao and other cave communities all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua of Bozhou raised a force at Rong Mountain. Ang led troops against him, annihilated his band, and every cave community of the Shan Yao, Mumao, Tuliao, and related peoples submitted.

sentences.zh: 十六年，以諸洞酋入朝，帝賜金綺衣、鞍轡，進安遠大將軍。

translations.literal: In year sixteen he led the chiefs of various caves to court; the Emperor granted gold brocade robes and saddlery and promoted him to Grand General of Pacifying the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he led the tribal chiefs to court. The Emperor granted him brocade robes of gold thread and full saddlery, and promoted him to Grand General of Pacifying the Distance.

sentences.zh: 徇沅州西南界，復新化、安仁二縣，擒劇賊張虎，縱之曰：「汝非吾敵，願降即來，不然，吾复擒汝不難也。」

translations.literal: He swept Yuan prefecture's southwestern border, recovered Xinhua and Anren counties, captured the fierce bandit Zhang Hu, released him and said: "You are not my match—if you wish to submit, come; otherwise capturing you again will not be hard."
translations.idiomatic: He marched through the southwest marches of Yuanzhou, recovered Xinhua and Anren counties, and captured the notorious bandit Zhang Hu. He released him with the words: "You are no match for me. Submit if you wish, and come in. Otherwise I can capture you again with ease."

sentences.zh: 明日，虎降，併其眾三千餘人，悉使歸民籍。

translations.literal: The next day Hu submitted; he incorporated his band of over three thousand men and all were restored to civilian registers.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zhang Hu surrendered with his force of more than three thousand men. Ang enrolled them all in the civilian registers.

sentences.zh: 軍還，眾斂白金以獻，一無所受。

translations.literal: When the army returned the troops collected white gold to present—and he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, his men pooled white silver as a gift, but he refused every coin.

sentences.zh: 行至江陵，眾復從致金而去，昂悉上之行省，宰臣令藏於庫，以示諸將。

translations.literal: When he reached Jiangling the troops again presented gold as he departed; Ang remitted all to the branch secretariat; the chief minister ordered it stored in the treasury to show the generals.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangling his troops again tried to give him gold as he departed. He sent the whole sum to the branch secretariat; the chief minister ordered it placed in the treasury as an example to the other generals.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，江西盜起，昂討之，進逼南安明揚、上龍、岩湖、綠村、石門、雁湖、赤水、黑風峒諸蠻，立太平寨而還。

translations.literal: In year twenty-six bandits rose in Jiangxi; Ang suppressed them, pressed forward against the Nan'an Mingyang, Shanglong, Yanhu, Lucun, Shimen, Yanhu, Chishui, Heifeng Cave and other barbarians, established Taiping stockade, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year rebels broke out in Jiangxi. Ang marched against them, pushed deep into the territories of the Mingyang, Shanglong, Yanhu, Lucun, Shimen, Yanhu, Chishui, Heifeng Cave, and other tribes of Nan'an, established Taiping stockade, and returned.

sentences.zh: 會大饑，以賊酋家資分賑之。

translations.literal: Meeting with great famine he distributed the bandit chiefs' household assets in relief.
translations.idiomatic: A great famine struck the region, and he distributed the rebel chiefs' seized property as famine relief.

sentences.zh: 授萬戶，賜金虎符，鎮撫州。

translations.literal: He was appointed myriarch, granted a gold tiger tally, and garrisoned Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made myriarch with a gold tiger tally and posted to garrison Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，省檄昂赴廣東監造戰船，行至廣東界，遇盜，移檄諭以禍福。

translations.literal: Before long the secretariat dispatched Ang to Guangdong to supervise building war vessels; reaching the Guangdong border he encountered bandits and sent a proclamation explaining fortunes and misfortunes.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the secretariat ordered him to Guangdong to supervise the construction of warships. At the Guangdong border he encountered bandits and sent them a proclamation on the consequences of submission and rebellion.

sentences.zh: 廣東素服其威信，及見其檄，即俱降。

translations.literal: Guangdong had long respected his authority and reputation; on seeing his proclamation they all at once submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong had long respected his authority. When they saw his proclamation, they surrendered at once.

sentences.zh: 授廣東宣慰使，卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: He was appointed Guangdong pacification commissioner, died, age sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed pacification commissioner of Guangdong and died at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 子震，杭州路鎮守萬戶。

translations.literal: His son Zhen was garrison myriarch of Hangzhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen served as garrison myriarch of Hangzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 惠，僉江西廉訪司事。

translations.literal: Hui was concurrent commissioner of the Jiangxi Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui served concurrently on the Jiangxi Surveillance Commission.

sentences.zh: 豫，知寧都州。

translations.literal: Yu was prefect of Ningdu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu was prefect of Ningdu.

sentences.zh: ○綦公直

translations.literal: Qi Gongzhi
translations.idiomatic: Qi Gongzhi

sentences.zh: 綦公直，益都樂安人，世業農。

translations.literal: Qi Gongzhi was a native of Le'an in Yidu; his family for generations farmed.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Gongzhi was a native of Le'an in Yidu. His family had farmed for generations.

sentences.zh: 至元五年，為益都勸農官。

translations.literal: In Zhiyuan 5 he was Yidu agricultural promotion officer.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 5 he served as agricultural promotion officer of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 九年，為沂、莒、膠、密、寧海五州都城池所千戶。

translations.literal: In year nine he was chiliarch of the capital wall and moat office of the five prefectures Yi, Ju, Jiao, Mi, and Ninghai.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was made chiliarch of the capital fortifications office for the five prefectures of Yi, Ju, Jiao, Mi, and Ninghai.

sentences.zh: 十年，賜金符，命造徵日本戰船於高麗。

translations.literal: In year ten he was granted a gold tally and ordered to build war ships for the expedition against Japan in Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he received a gold tally and was ordered to build warships for the Japan expedition in Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 時宋未下，世祖知其勇，遣使召見，俾與乎不烈拔都等領兵，同行荊南等處招討司事。

translations.literal: When Song was not yet taken Kublai knew his bravery, sent envoys to summon and see him, and had him with Hubilie Batu and others lead troops and jointly hold the office of Pacification Commissioner of Jingnan and other regions.
translations.idiomatic: Song had not yet fallen. Kublai, knowing his courage, summoned him to court and ordered him, together with Hubilie Batu and others, to lead troops and serve jointly as pacification commissioner for Jingnan and adjacent territories.

sentences.zh: 抵峽州青草灘，霖雨，不進，還屯玉泉山。

translations.literal: Reaching Qingcao Beach in Xia prefecture, heavy rains—no advance; he returned to encamp at Yuquan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: At Qingcao Beach in Xizhou, heavy rains halted the advance, and he withdrew to encamp on Yuquan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 率兵三千攻安進下寨，破之，殺宋軍百餘人，獲牛馬七百。

translations.literal: He led three thousand troops to attack Anjin Lower Stockade, broke it, killed over a hundred Song troops, and captured seven hundred oxen and horses.
translations.idiomatic: He led three thousand men against Anjin Lower Stockade, captured it, killed more than a hundred Song soldiers, and took seven hundred head of cattle and horses.

sentences.zh: 還至襄陽，樞密院命督造戰艦、運舟。

translations.literal: Returning to Xiangyang the Secretariat for Military Affairs ordered him to supervise building warships and transport boats.
translations.idiomatic: Back at Xiangyang, the Secretariat for Military Affairs put him in charge of building warships and transport vessels.

sentences.zh: 襄陽既下，奉旨領鄭州、光化、唐州漢軍，及郢、复熟券軍九千二百人，從諸軍南伐。

translations.literal: After Xiangyang fell he received an edict to lead Han troops of Zheng, Guanghua, and Tang prefectures and nine thousand two hundred seasoned troops of Ying and Fu with draft certificates, following the various armies south to conquer.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiangyang fell, he was ordered to lead the Han armies of Zhengzhou, Guanghua, and Tangzhou, together with nine thousand two hundred veteran troops of Yingzhou and Fuzhou under the draft-certificate system, on the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 十二年冬，至隆興。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, winter, he reached Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the twelfth year he reached Longxing.

sentences.zh: 宋軍突出城門逆戰，公直敗之，追抵城下，遂逾壕拔木，焚其樓櫓，斬首萬餘級，生擒七百人，隆興降。

translations.literal: Song troops sallied from the gates to meet battle; Gongzhi defeated them, pursued to the wall, then crossed the moat and pulled up timber, burned their towers and palisades, beheaded over ten thousand heads, took seven hundred alive, and Longxing submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Song forces charged out of the gates to give battle. Gongzhi routed them, pursued to the walls, crossed the moat, tore out the palisades, burned the towers, took more than ten thousand heads and seven hundred prisoners, and Longxing surrendered.

sentences.zh: 由是南安、吉、贛皆望風款附，平堡柵六百餘所。

translations.literal: From this Nan'an, Ji, and Gan all upon seeing the wind came offering allegiance; he pacified over six hundred fort stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Nan'an, Ji, and Gan submitted one after another. He pacified more than six hundred fortified stockades.

sentences.zh: 公直又令第三子忙古台攻梅關，破淮德山寨，入廣東，至南海，皆下之。

translations.literal: Gongzhi also ordered his third son Mangutai to attack Mei Pass, break Huai De Mountain stockade, enter Guangdong, reach the South Sea—all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhi sent his third son Mangutai to storm Mei Pass, break Huai De Mountain stockade, advance into Guangdong as far as the South Sea, and seize every stronghold along the way.

sentences.zh: 詔授公直武毅將軍、管軍上千戶。

translations.literal: By edict Gongzhi was appointed General of Martial Steadfastness and senior chiliarch commanding troops.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Gongzhi General of Martial Steadfastness and senior chiliarch commanding troops.

sentences.zh: 召入，加昭勇大將軍、管軍萬戶，佩金虎符，領侍衛親軍。

translations.literal: Summoned to court, he was promoted to Grand General of Manifest Valor and myriarch commanding troops, wore a gold tiger tally, and led the imperial guard corps.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court, he was promoted to Grand General of Manifest Valor and army myriarch, given a gold tiger tally, and placed in command of the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 時伯延伯答罕、禿忽魯叛於西夏，命公直率軍討平之。

translations.literal: At that time Boyan Bodahan and Tuhulu rebelled in Western Xia; Gongzhi was ordered to lead troops to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: When Boyan Bodahan and Tuhulu rebelled in Western Xia, Gongzhi was ordered to lead troops against them and restore order.

sentences.zh: 十八年五月，升輔國上將軍、都元帥、宣慰使，鎮別十八里。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of year eighteen he was promoted to Supporter of the State General-in-Chief, grand general, and pacification commissioner, garrisoning Bie Shibali.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighteenth year he was promoted to Supporter of the State General-in-Chief, grand general, and pacification commissioner, and posted to Bie Shibali.

sentences.zh: 初，帝詔以子泰襲萬戶。

translations.literal: Initially the Emperor edicted that his son Tai inherit the myriarchy.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Emperor had decreed that his son Tai should inherit the myriarchy.

sentences.zh: 公直自陳父年老，乞以泰為樂安縣尹，就養其父，制可，仍終身勿徙他職。

translations.literal: Gongzhi personally stated his father was old, begged that Tai be made magistrate of Le'an county to go nourish his father—the rescript approved, still for life not transferred to another office.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhi petitioned that his father was elderly and asked that Tai be appointed magistrate of Le'an county so he could care for him at home. The court approved and decreed that Tai should hold no other post for life.

sentences.zh: 至是，乃以忙古台襲萬戶，佩金虎符，從之鎮。

translations.literal: At this time Mangutai inherited the myriarchy, wore a gold tiger tally, and followed him to garrison.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion Mangutai inherited the myriarchy with a gold tiger tally and accompanied him to his posting.

sentences.zh: 公直陛辭，曰：「臣父喪五年，願葬以行。」

translations.literal: Gongzhi took leave at court audience and said: "My father's mourning is five years; I wish to bury him before departing."
translations.idiomatic: Taking leave at court, Gongzhi said: "My father died five years ago. I ask leave to perform his burial before I march."

sentences.zh: 帝許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 至家，葬事畢，遂計樂安稅課及貧民逋負，悉以賜金代輸之，乃行。

translations.literal: Reaching home, when burial was complete he reckoned Le'an tax levies and poor people's arrears and fully used granted gold to pay them in their stead, then departed.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home and completing the funeral, he calculated Le'an's tax assessments and the tax arrears of the poor, paid them all from his own gold stipend, and then set out.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，諸王海都叛，侵別十八里，公直從丞相伯顏進戰於洪水山，敗之。

translations.literal: In year twenty-three Prince Khaydu rebelled, invaded Bie Shibali; Gongzhi followed Chancellor Bayan in advancing to battle at Hongshui Mountain and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year Prince Khaydu rebelled and invaded Bie Shibali. Gongzhi joined Chancellor Bayan in battle at Hongshui Mountain and defeated the rebels.

sentences.zh: 追擊浸遠，援兵不至，第五子瑗力戰而死，公直與妻及忙古台俱陷焉。

translations.literal: Pursuit went ever farther; reinforcements did not arrive; his fifth son Yuan fought fiercely and died; Gongzhi with his wife and Mangutai were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit carried them too far and reinforcements never came. His fifth son Yuan fought to the death. Gongzhi, his wife, and Mangutai were all captured.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，忙古台奔還，授定遠大將軍、中侍衛親軍副都指揮使，改湖州砲手軍匠萬戶。

translations.literal: In year twenty-four Mangutai fled back; he was appointed Grand General of Settling the Distance, vice commander of the Central Imperial Guard Corps, and transferred to myriarch of Huzhou artillery and military craftsmen.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year Mangutai escaped and returned. He was made Grand General of Settling the Distance, vice commander of the Central Imperial Guard, and transferred to myriarch of the Huzhou artillery and military craftsmen corps.

sentences.zh: 討衢州山賊，有功，加昭勇大將軍。

translations.literal: Suppressing Quzhou mountain bandits he had merit and was promoted to Grand General of Manifest Valor.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed mountain bandits in Quzhou with distinction and was promoted to Grand General of Manifest Valor.

sentences.zh: 泰後終於知寧海州。

translations.literal: Tai later ended as prefect of Ninghai prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tai later served to the end as prefect of Ninghai.

sentences.zh: ○楊賽因不花

translations.literal: Yangsaiyinbuhua
translations.idiomatic: Yangsaiyinbuhua

sentences.zh: 楊賽因不花，初名漢英，字熙載，賽因不花，賜名也。

translations.literal: Yangsaiyinbuhua—his original name Hanying, style Xizai; Saiyinbuhua was a granted name.
translations.idiomatic: Yangsaiyinbuhua was originally named Hanying, courtesy name Xizai. Saiyinbuhua was the name granted him by the throne.

sentences.zh: 其先太原人。

translations.literal: His ancestors were men of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His family came originally from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 唐季南詔陷播州，有楊端者，以應募起，竟復播州，遂使領之。

translations.literal: In the late Tang the Nanzhao took Bozhou; there was a Yang Duan who rose by answering recruitment, finally recovered Bozhou, and was then made to lead it.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Tang the Nanzhao seized Bozhou. A Yang Duan answered the recruitment call, eventually recovered Bozhou, and was put in charge of the region.

sentences.zh: 五代以來，世襲其職。

translations.literal: From the Five Dynasties onward they hereditarily inherited the office.
translations.idiomatic: From the Five Dynasties onward the family held the post in hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 五傳至昭，無子，以族子貴遷嗣。

translations.literal: Five generations passed to Zhao; having no son, a clansman's son Guiqian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The line passed through five generations to Zhao, who had no son. A clansman's son, Guiqian, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 又八傳至粲，粲生價，價生文，文生邦憲，皆仕宋，為播​​州安撫使。

translations.literal: Eight more generations passed to Can; Can begat Jia, Jia begat Wen, Wen begat Bangxian—all served Song as Pacification Commissioners of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Eight generations later the line reached Can. Can's son Jia was followed by Wen and then Bangxian; all served the Song as pacification commissioners of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 至元十三年，宋亡，世祖詔諭之，邦憲奉版籍內附，授龍虎衛上將軍、紹慶珍州南平等處沿邊宣慰使、播州安撫使，卒，年四十三，贈推忠效順功臣、平章政事，追封播國公，諡惠敏。

translations.literal: In Zhiyuan 13 Song perished; Kublai edicted and instructed them; Bangxian presented registers and came within; he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Dragon-Tiger Guard, Pacification Commissioner along the borders of Shaoqing, Zhen, Nanping and other places, and Pacification Commissioner of Bozhou; died, age forty-three; posthumously granted the merit title Loyal and Obedient Merit Subject and Grand Councillor, posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Bo State, temple name Huimin.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 13 Song fell. Kublai issued an edict to the family, and Bangxian submitted the prefectural registers and joined the dynasty. He was appointed General-in-Chief of the Dragon-Tiger Guard, Pacification Commissioner for the border districts of Shaoqing, Zhen, Nanping, and adjacent territories, and Pacification Commissioner of Bozhou. He died at forty-three. Posthumously he was granted the title Merit Subject of Loyal Submission and Minister of State, enfeoffed as Duke of Bo, with the temple name Huimin.

sentences.zh: 漢英，邦憲子也，生五歲而父卒。

translations.literal: Hanying was Bangxian's son; at five years old his father died.
translations.idiomatic: Hanying was Bangxian's son. He was five years old when his father died.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，母田氏攜至上京，見世祖於大安閣。

translations.literal: In year twenty-two Lady Tian his mother brought him to the Upper Capital; he saw Kublai at the Great Tranquility Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year his mother, Lady Tian, brought him to the Upper Capital, where he was received by Kublai at the Great Tranquility Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 帝呼至禦榻前，熟視其眸子，撫其頂者久之，乃諭宰臣曰：「楊氏母子孤寡，萬里來庭，朕甚憫之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor called him before the imperial couch, looked long and closely at his eyes, and stroked his head for a long while before instructing the chief ministers: "The Yang mother and son are alone and bereft; they have come ten thousand li to court—I deeply pity them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned him to the imperial couch, studied his eyes at length, and stroked his head for a long while before telling the chief ministers: "The Yang mother and son are alone and bereft. They have traveled ten thousand li to come before the throne, and I am deeply moved to pity them.

sentences.zh: 遂命襲父職，錫金虎符，因賜名賽因不花。

translations.literal: He was thereupon ordered to inherit his father's post, granted a gold tiger tally, and given the name Saiyinbuhua.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon ordered to inherit his father's post, granted a gold tiger tally, and given the name Saiyinbuhua.

sentences.zh: 及陛辭，詔中書錫宴，賜金幣彩繒，賚其從者有差。

translations.literal: When he took leave at court, an edict ordered the Secretariat to grant a banquet, bestow gold, coins, and colored silks, and reward his followers in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: On taking leave, the court ordered the Secretariat to host a banquet and bestow gold, coins, and brocades; his attendants were rewarded according to rank.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，再入覲，時年十二，帝見其應對明敏，稱善者三。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he entered court again; he was then twelve years old. The Emperor saw his replies were clear and quick and praised him three times.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-five he came to court again at age twelve. Kublai found his answers sharp and praised him three times.

sentences.zh: 復因宰臣奏安邊事，帝益嘉之。

translations.literal: Again when the chief ministers memorialized on securing the borders, the Emperor praised him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief ministers reported on border security, the Khan praised him still more.

sentences.zh: 是年，改安撫司為宣撫司，授宣撫使，尋升侍衛親軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: That year the pacification office was changed to a pacification commission office; he was appointed pacification commissioner, and soon promoted to commander-in-chief of the personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: That year the pacification office became a pacification commission; he was made commissioner and soon commander-in-chief of the personal guard.

sentences.zh: ○鮮卑仲吉

translations.literal: Xianbei Zhongji
translations.idiomatic: Xianbei Zhongji

sentences.zh: 鮮卑仲吉，中山人。

translations.literal: Xianbei Zhongji was a native of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Xianbei Zhongji came from Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 歲乙亥，國兵定中原，仲吉首率平灤路軍民詣軍門降，太祖命為灤州節度使。

translations.literal: In the year yihai the imperial army pacified the Central Plain; Zhongji was first to lead the military and civilians of Pingluan circuit to the army gate to surrender. Taizu appointed him military commissioner of Luan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the yihai year, as the imperial armies pacified the north, Zhongji was first to lead Pingluan's forces to surrender. Genghis Khan made him military commissioner of Luanzhou.

sentences.zh: 從阿術魯南征，充右副元帥，攻取信安、關州諸城，以功賜虎符，授河北等路漢軍兵馬都元帥。

translations.literal: He followed Artsur on the southern campaign, served as right deputy marshal, attacked and took Xin'an, Guan prefecture, and other cities; for merit he was granted a tiger tally and appointed commander-in-chief of Han army troops and horses of Hebei and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned south under Artsur as right deputy marshal, took Xin'an, Guanzhou, and other cities, and was rewarded with a tiger tally and command of Hebei Han forces.

sentences.zh: 歲壬辰，平蔡有功，加金吾衛上將軍、興平路都元帥、右監軍、永安軍節度使，兼灤州管內觀察使、提舉常平倉事、開國侯，尋卒。

translations.literal: In the year renchen he had merit in pacifying Cai; he was promoted to Superior General of the Golden Guard, commander-in-chief of Xingping circuit, right army inspector, military commissioner of Yong'an Army, concurrently observation commissioner within Luan prefecture, commissioner for the ever-normal granaries, and Marquis Who Founded the State; soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the renchen year he helped pacify Cai and was made Superior General of the Golden Guard, Xingping commander-in-chief, right army inspector, Yong'an military commissioner, Luan observation commissioner, and founding marquis before his death.

sentences.zh: 子誠襲，授宣武將軍、高郵上萬戶府副萬戶，佩虎符，改授懷遠大將軍、僉武衛親軍都指揮使司事。

translations.literal: His son Cheng inherited; he was appointed General of Manifest Martiality and deputy ten-thousand-household of the Gaoyou superior ten-thousand-household office, wearing a tiger tally, then reassigned as Great General of Cherishing the Distant and commissioner of the Martial Guard personal army headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cheng inherited, became General of Manifest Martiality and deputy myriarch at Gaoyou with a tiger tally, then Great General of Cherishing the Distant and commissioner of the Martial Guard headquarters.

sentences.zh: 領兵徵爪哇，攻八百媳婦國，使廣東，克勤於役，尋以疾卒。

translations.literal: He led troops on the Java expedition, attacked the Kingdom of Eight Hundred Wives, and was dispatched to Guangdong; diligent in service, he soon died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops against Java and the Kingdom of Eight Hundred Wives and served in Guangdong with tireless diligence before dying of illness.

sentences.zh: 子忽篤土襲。

translations.literal: His son Hudutu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hudutu inherited the post.

sentences.zh: ○完顏石柱

translations.literal: Wanyan Shizhu
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Shizhu

sentences.zh: 完顏石柱，祖德住，仕金為管軍千戶。

translations.literal: Wanyan Shizhu—his grandfather Dezhu served the Jin as army chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Shizhu's grandfather Dezhu had served the Jin as an army chiliarch.

sentences.zh: 父拿住，歸太祖，從征西域、河西，又從太宗攻下鳳翔、同州，有功，賜號八都兒，佩銀符，為同州管民達魯花赤，改賜金符，兼徵行千戶，總管八都軍。

translations.literal: His father Nazhu submitted to Taizu, followed campaigns in the Western Regions and Hexi, and again followed Taizong in taking Fengxiang and Tong prefecture, having merit. He was granted the title Badu'er, wore a silver tally, served as darughachi governing the people of Tong prefecture, was changed to a gold tally, and concurrently made campaign chiliarch commanding the Badu army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Nazhu submitted to Genghis Khan, campaigned in the west and Hexi, and helped Taizong take Fengxiang and Tongzhou. Named Badu'er, he became Tongzhou's darughachi with silver then gold tally and commanded the Badu army as campaign chiliarch.

sentences.zh: 憲宗以拿住年老，命石柱襲其職。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong, because Nazhu was old, ordered Shizhu to inherit his post.
translations.idiomatic: When Nazhu grew old, Emperor Möngke had Shizhu inherit his post.

sentences.zh: 己未，石柱從世祖徵合剌章還，都元帥紐璘攻馬湖江，石柱奪浮橋，與宋兵戰，有功，賞白金七百五十兩。

translations.literal: In jiwei Shizhu followed Emperor Shizu on the campaign against Helazhang and returned. Commander-in-chief Niulun attacked the Mahu River; Shizhu seized the pontoon bridge and fought Song troops, having merit, and was rewarded with seven hundred fifty liang of white gold.
translations.idiomatic: In jiwei (1259) Shizhu followed Kublai against Helazhang. When Niulun attacked the Mahu River, Shizhu seized the pontoon bridge, fought Song forces, and was rewarded with seven hundred fifty liang of silver.

sentences.zh: 軍隆化縣，與宋兵戰，大敗之。

translations.literal: The army was at Longhua county; he fought Song troops and defeated them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: At Longhua county he fought Song forces and routed them.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，授徵行萬戶，佩金符。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong he was appointed campaign ten-thousand-household and wore a gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongtong 2 he was made campaign myriarch with a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 三年，從都元帥帖哥攻嘉定，有功，改賜金虎符。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed Commander-in-chief Tiege in attacking Jiading, had merit, and was granted a gold tiger tally in exchange.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he fought under Commander-in-chief Tiege at Jiading and received a gold tiger tally for his service.

sentences.zh: 至元四年，敗宋兵於九頂山，生獲四十餘人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhiyuan he defeated Song troops at Jiuding Mountain and captured more than forty alive.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 4 he defeated Song forces at Jiuding Mountain and took over forty prisoners.

sentences.zh: 五年，攻瀘州之水寨，擊五獲寨，渡馬湖江，迎擊宋兵，敗之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he attacked the water stockade at Luzhou, struck Wuhuo stockade, crossed the Mahu River, met and struck Song troops, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he attacked Luzhou's river stockade and Wuhuo stockade, crossed the Mahu River, and routed Song forces.

sentences.zh: 從行省也速帶兒攻建都，建都降，從攻嘉定，复瀘州，取重慶，石柱之功居多。

translations.literal: He followed the regional secretariat's Yesudai'er in attacking Jiandu; Jiandu surrendered. He followed attacks on Jiading, recovered Luzhou, and took Chongqing—Shizhu's merit was the greater part.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Yesudai'er against Jiandu until it surrendered, then helped retake Jiading and Luzhou and capture Chongqing—Shizhu's contribution was the greatest.

sentences.zh: 十四年，遷昭勇大將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Great General of Manifest Valor.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen he was made Great General of Manifest Valor.

sentences.zh: 十六年，授四川東道宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was appointed pacification envoy of the eastern Sichuan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In year sixteen he became eastern Sichuan pacification envoy.

sentences.zh: 十七年，改鎮國上將軍、四川西道宣慰使，總管隨路八都萬戶。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was changed to Suppressing-the-State Superior General and pacification envoy of the western Sichuan circuit, commanding the Badu ten-thousand-households of each circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In year seventeen he became Suppressing-the-State Superior General and western Sichuan pacification envoy, commanding the circuit Badu myriarchs.

sentences.zh: 二十年，拜四川行省參知政事，卒。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was appointed associate administrator of the Sichuan Regional Secretariat and died.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty he was made associate administrator of the Sichuan Secretariat and died.

sentences.zh: 弟真童，襲為隨路八都萬戶。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhentong inherited as Badu ten-thousand-household of each circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhentong inherited the circuit Badu myriarch post.
